author: junebug-junie
body:
### Motivation
- Improve observability across RPC hops to help diagnose `RPC timeout` and slow/failing services.  
- Record elapsed time and error context for `bus.rpc_request` and reply `publish` calls to identify slow/failed RPCs.  
- Surface publish lifecycle problems and missing reply channels for the Landing Pad RPC server.  
- Capture timing for Landing Pad and State RPCs used by metacognition context assembly to aid debugging of trace mismatches.

### Description
- Instrumented RPC clients in `services/orion-cortex-exec/app/clients.py` to measure elapsed time around `bus.rpc_request` and emit `RPC ok <-` / `RPC error <-` logs including `correlation_id` and `reply` context.  
- Added timing and success/failure logging for Landing Pad and State calls in the metacognition context step in `services/orion-cortex-exec/app/executor.py`.  
- Logged elapsed time and handled publish errors for exec reply publishing in `services/orion-cortex-exec/app/main.py`, and added a warning when `reply_to` is missing.  
- Enhanced `services/orion-landing-pad/app/rpc/server.py` to log decode failures, incoming request metadata, response publish failures (with elapsed time), and warn when `reply_channel` is missing.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes.

author: grownup-nimbi
body:
## What was changed
Added a repository-level `.editorconfig` file that enforces consistent formatting rules across editors and operating systems. This includes:
- LF line endings
- final newline insertion
- trimming trailing whitespace (except Markdown)
- Go files using tabs (Go convention)
- YAML/JSON using 2-space indentation

## Why it was changed
Formatting differences (especially line endings and whitespace) create noisy diffs and make reviews harder. Go projects also benefit from explicit “tabs for .go files” rules to match typical Go formatting expectations. A shared EditorConfig reduces accidental style drift and keeps the repository consistent across contributors.

## Test
1. Open a `.go` file in your editor, add a small change, and save.
2. Confirm indentation for Go files is tabs (not spaces) and line endings are LF.
3. Open a `.yml` / `.yaml` / `.json` file, make a small change, and save.
4. Confirm those files use 2-space indentation, and trailing whitespace is removed.
5. Open a Markdown file and confirm trailing whitespace is not forcibly trimmed (to preserve intentional line breaks).

body:
The codebase had 14 TypeScript compilation errors preventing builds: type incompatibilities in command definitions and null safety violations in guild access patterns.

## Changes

**Type system fixes**
- Added `SlashCommandOptionsOnlyBuilder` to `Command` interface's data union type
- Discord.js returns this type when adding options to `SlashCommandBuilder`, but the interface didn't accept it

**Null safety**
- Added non-null assertions on `interaction.guild` access (6 locations)
- All locations already guard with `interaction.guildId` check, making assertions safe

**Import cleanup**
- Removed unused `ChatInputCommandInteraction` type imports (12 files)
- Removed unused `logger` import from permissions checks
- Removed unused `services` parameter from commands that don't need it

```typescript
// Before: Type error on commands with options
export interface Command {
  data: SlashCommandBuilder | SlashCommandSubcommandsOnlyBuilder;
}

// After: Accepts builder with options
export interface Command {
  data: SlashCommandBuilder 
    | SlashCommandSubcommandsOnlyBuilder 
    | SlashCommandOptionsOnlyBuilder
    | Omit<SlashCommandBuilder, 'addSubcommand' | 'addSubcommandGroup'>;
}
```

author: hgqxjj
body:
Please review this change. Thanks! **Description:** When -XX:+PrintDeoptimizationDetails is enabled, vframeArray.cpp prints interpreted frames under ttyLocker. https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/578204f8c49f06be8b9c4855359ca61c9e107678/src/hotspot/share/runtime/vframeArray.cpp#L493-L503 In the WizardMode && Verbose branch it calls Method::print_codes() / print_codes_on(). The bytecode printing path may acquire MDOExtraData_lock (rank nosafepoint-1). https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/578204f8c49f06be8b9c4855359ca61c9e107678/src/hotspot/share/interpreter/bytecodeTracer.cpp#L597-L602 Calling it while holding tty_lock violates the global lock ranking order and triggers a lock rank inversion assertion. **Fix:** Generate the bytecode dump before taking tty_lock, and print it afterwards under ttyLocker to keep the output coherent while preserving correct lock acquisition order. To avoid double buffering when the target stream is already a thread-local stringStream, extend BytecodeTracer::print_method_codes with a buffered flag . The new call site uses buffered=false when dumping into the temporary stringStream. **Test:** GHA --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - [x] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8374862](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8374862): assert(false) failed: Attempting to acquire lock MDOExtraData_lock/nosafepoint-1 out of order with lock tty_lock/tty -- possible deadlock (running with -XX:+Verbose -XX:+WizardMode -XX:+PrintDeoptimizationDetails) (**Bug** - P4) ### Reviewers * [David Holmes](https://openjdk.org/census#dholmes) (@dholmes-ora - **Reviewer**) * [Dean Long](https://openjdk.org/census#dlong) (@dean-long - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewing

author: fw-bot
body:
This commit upgrades our PDF/A compliance from 3B to 3A, and fixes a few issues previously undetected due to the different PyPDF libraries we're currently supporting that made the previous PDF fails even the 3B validation.

Improvement 1:

PDFA validators were previously detecting our file as 3B. Hence we update the metadata content `conformance` to `A`.

Issue 2:

When using `._pypdf` library, we failed the 6.1.2-2 and 6.8-1 rule even
though we have implemented them on the previous version. It seems that
this is caused by the `if SUBMOD...` check only ensuring it's not equal
to `_pypdf2_2` (which makes it trigger for the new `_pypdf`). Hence, we
reclarify the comments and fix the IF check.


Issue 3:

After implementing issue 2, it seems that a traceback occurs every time we're using `._pypdf` and calling the pdf write method. This is because the added characters on the header can't be decoded with `UTF-8`. Hence we change it to other greater-than-127-bytes characters that can still be decoded with `UTF-8`. (The actual character used here doesn't matter).

Improvement 4:

To be compliant with the new 3A rules (additional rules not there in 3B when we first implemented them), we add a minimal mark info dictionary and document structure on the PDF catalog object (`_root_object`).

author: copilot
body:
Transforms Codeforces problems into LeetCode-style format with OOP C++ signatures using Google's Gemini API. Pure format conversion—no search, matching, or external problem fetching.

## Changes

**New Components**
- `geminiService.ts`: DOM extraction from CF problem page + Gemini API integration
- `LCFormatPanel.tsx`: Left-side collapsible panel (45% width, theme-aware, slide animations)
  - Copy to clipboard with visual feedback
  - Download as JSON
  - Responsive scrollable content

**Integration**
- `TopBar.tsx`: FileCode2 button (disabled when no problem loaded)
- `page.tsx`: Handler orchestration with toast notifications
- `useCFStore.ts`: Added `geminiApiKey` state (localStorage-backed, default provided)
- `main.tsx`: Sonner toaster for user feedback

## API Flow

```typescript
// Extract problem from active CF tab
const problemText = await extractCFProblem();

// Transform via Gemini 1.5 Flash
const lcFormat = await convertCFtoLC(problemText, apiKey);
// Returns: { title, difficulty, description, functionSignature, 
//           constraints[], examples[], testCaseFormat }
```

DOM extraction targets `.problem-statement` with specific traversal to avoid over-broad selectors. API key stored in config (not hardcoded) with localStorage fallback.

## Output Format

```json
{
  "title": "Clean Problem Title",
  "difficulty": "Medium",
  "functionSignature": "class Solution {\npublic:\n    RetType solve(params) {...}\n};",
  "constraints": ["1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5"],
  "examples": [{"input": "...", "output": "...", "explanation": "..."}]
}
```

Panel renders at z-index 1000, doesn't interfere with editor. All UI elements adapt to dark/light theme automatically.

author: wenyxu
body:
I hereby agree to the terms of the [GreptimeDB CLA](https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/.github/blob/main/CLA.md).

## Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional)
#6558 
## What's changed and what's your intention?

This PR introduces support for repartitioning Metric Engine tables and refines the repartition procedure's state machine. It implements a dedicated `SyncRegion` instruction for logical regions synchronization and refines the region state transitions during the repartition process.

### Changes
**Metric Engine Repartition Support**
- Internal Column Handling: Updated `build_template_from_raw_table_info` to optionally filter out metric engine internal columns. This ensures that when creating new regions during repartition, internal columns are handled correctly based on the engine type.
- Physical/Logical Table Support: Added logic to handle repartitioning (Split/Merge) on physical metric tables, ensuring proper interaction with associated logical tables.
- New SyncRegion Instruction: Introduced a specific instruction and handler (`SyncRegionHandler`) to synchronize logical regions from central region.
- State Machine Refactoring:
  - Integrated `SyncRegion` into the repartition group procedure.
  - Added a new `ExitStaging` state to `UpdateMetadata` to explicitly clear staging leader information after a successful repartition.
  - Refine the execution flow: SyncRegion -> EnterStaging -> ApplyStaging ... -> ExitStaging.

**Region State Management**
- Mito2 State Transition: Modified `set_dropping` to accept an expected previous state (either Writable or Staging). This fixes issues when dropping regions that are currently in the staging state during repartition.

**Tests & Observability**
- Integration Tests: Added SQL integration tests covering SPLIT PARTITION and MERGE PARTITION for metric engine tables, verifying data consistency across physical and logical tables.
- Logging: Enhanced logging throughout the repartition procedure (state transitions, instruction dispatching, and table route updates) for better debugging and observability.

## PR Checklist
Please convert it to a draft if some of the following conditions are not met.

- [ ] I have written the necessary rustdoc comments.
- [ ] I have added the necessary unit tests and integration tests.
- [ ] This PR requires documentation updates.
- [ ] API changes are backward compatible.
- [ ] Schema or data changes are backward compatible.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Enables repartition (split/merge) for metric engine tables and adds region sync orchestration in the repartition pipeline.
> 
> - Adds `SyncRegion` instruction (request/reply types) and datanode `SyncRegionHandler`; wires through heartbeat handler and instruction dispatch/replies
> - Integrates region sync into group procedure: flush central region → `SyncRegion` → enter staging → apply staging → exit staging; adds `ExitStaging` metadata update state
> - Updates template building: `build_template_from_raw_table_info(raw_table_info, skip_internal_columns)` to optionally filter metric-engine internal columns; callers updated
> - Refactors flush logic into `procedure::utils::flush_region` and enhances logging across repartition states/handlers
> - Mito2: `set_dropping(expect_state)` to allow dropping from `Writable` or `Staging`; drop/copy handlers accept staging contexts
> - Store API: make `SyncRegionFromRequest` serializable/deserializable
> - Tests: add integration tests for metric-engine repartition (split/merge) and unit tests for sync handler/flows; extend mocks to support sync-region
>

author: futuroptimist
body:
### Motivation

- Custom processes were rendered as "reference only" and did not expose start/pause/cancel/finish controls, causing the UI to differ from built-in processes.
- Game-state helpers looked up process definitions only in the built-in catalog, so actions could not operate on runtime `processData` for custom entries.
- The intent is to make the custom-process view behave identically to built-in processes once a custom process is created.

### Description

- Add `getProcessDefinition` and allow game-state helpers to accept an optional `processDefinition` parameter so `startProcess`, `cancelProcess`, `finishProcess`, `finishProcessNow`, and `hasRequiredAndConsumedItems` can operate on provided custom definitions instead of only `generated/processes.json`.
- Update `frontend/src/components/svelte/Process.svelte` to remove the reference-only note, render the same controls for custom processes, and pass `processData` into game-state calls when available so actions work for custom processes.
- Ensure the periodic state updater runs when a process is mounted so controls reflect current state for both built-in and custom processes.
- Update tests in `frontend/src/components/__tests__/Process.spec.ts` and `frontend/__tests__/ProcessCustom.test.js` to expect controls for custom processes and verify `startProcess` is invoked with the custom process definition.

### Testing

- No automated test suite was executed as part of this change (unit/E2E runs were not requested).
- Existing unit tests were updated to reflect the new behavior (files: `Process.spec.ts`, `ProcessCustom.test.js`) and should be run locally or in CI via `npm run test:ci`.
- Static checks (secret scan) were run against the staged diff with no issues reported.
- Manual smoke verification is recommended in CI where E2E and image smoke tests will validate SSR and runtime behavior.

| Stage | 모듈 | 역할 |
|-------|------|------|
| 1 | background_builder | OHLCV-only 배경 구간 탐지 |
| 2 | lh_builder + divergence_builder | L/H 피벗 + 다이버전스 |
| 3 | zone_builder + trend_builder | 배경 재점수화 |
| 4 | transition_builder + labeler + backtest_report | 최종 판단 |

### 운영 규칙 (고정, 변경 금지)
- `SCORE_THRESHOLD >= 4`
- `DULLING_RATIO = 0.5`
- `LABEL_HORIZON = 16`
- `LABEL_MIN_PCT = 0.003` (A/B 테스트 결과 채택)

---

### 1. Background Builder: Giant Zone 해결
| 항목 | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| bg_candidates | 1 | 16 |
| Giant zone | YES (67.8%) | NO (max 4.98%) |
| Zone widths | 67.8% | 1.19% - 4.98% |
| Total zones | 2 | 63 (16bg + 47LH) |

### 2. Labeler: LABEL_MIN_PCT 조정
| 항목 | Baseline (0.005) | 채택 (0.003) |
|------|------------------|--------------|
| Nothing% | 60.5% | 43.5% |
| Decisive% | 39.5% | 56.5% |
| Precision | 0.328 | 0.305 |
| Signal count | 494 | 494 (0% 감소) |

### 3. Transition Builder: Variant B Reversal 분류 채택

**A/B/C 실험 결과 (BTC 30k candles, TF=1):**

**Table 1: Summary per Variant**
| Variant | Total | TR_Rev | Cont | Bounce | Prec | B→B | B→B2 | Dec% | Noth% |
|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|------|-----|------|------|-------|
| A (baseline) | 494 | 3 | 240 | 251 | 0.3047 | 0.5373 | 0.4949 | 56.5 | 43.5 |
| **B (채택)** | **494** | **242** | **1** | **251** | **0.3047** | **0.5373** | **0.4949** | **56.5** | **43.5** |
| C | 494 | 18 | 225 | 251 | 0.3047 | 0.5373 | 0.4949 | 56.5 | 43.5 |

**Table 2: Baseline Deltas**
| Variant | ΔSignal | ΔTR_Rev | ΔPrec | ΔDec% | ΔNoth% |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|--------|
| A | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **B** | **0** | **+239** | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| C | 0 | +15 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Table 3: Reversal Quality**
| Variant | Rev_N | Rev_Conf | Rev_Den | Rev_Amb | Rev_Prec | Rev_MFE | Rev_MAE |
|---------|-------|----------|---------|---------|----------|---------|---------|
| A | 3 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 1.000 | 0.0117 | -0.0037 |
| **B** | **242** | **37** | **86** | **119** | **0.3008** | **0.0060** | **-0.0056** |
| C | 18 | 1 | 8 | 9 | 0.111 | 0.0048 | -0.0041 |

**Variant B 선택 근거 (5문장):**
1. Variant B는 reversal 조건을 AND에서 OR로 완화하여 trend_reversal 수를 3→242로 증가시킴.
2. 이는 새로운 조건을 추가하는 것이 아니라, 같은 score>=4 신호를 더 세밀하게 분류하는 것임 — 다이버전스 누적 OR 새 zone 출현 중 하나만 있어도 추세 약화와 결합 시 구조적 전환 근거로 인정.
3. 전체 신호 수는 494로 동일(0% 감소)하여 새로운 필터링이 도입되지 않음을 확인.
4. Reversal precision 0.3008, MFE 0.0060으로 재분류된 reversal이 의미 있는 전방 가격 움직임을 보임.
5. OR 완화는 신호를 만들어내지 않으며, 강한 구조적 근거가 있는 continuation 후보를 적절한 reversal 범주로 승격시킬 뿐임.

### 4. Backtest Report 확장
- `TransitionTypeMetrics` 추가: 타입별 precision/MFE/MAE 표시
- `DirectionalMetrics`: 방향별 분해 (bull→bear / bear→bull)
- decisive% / nothing% 표시

### 최종 검증 결과 (BTC-USDT 30k candles, TF=1)
```
Total candidates: 494, Labeled: 494
Precision: 0.3047, Decisive%: 56.5%, Nothing%: 43.5%
bull→bear prec: 0.5373, bear→bull prec: 0.4949
trend_reversal: 242 (prec=0.3008, MFE=0.0060)
single_bounce: 251 (prec=0.3077, MFE=0.0073)
Score 4: 475 (prec=0.299), Score 5: 19 (prec=0.500)
```

### 변경 파일
- `transition_builder.py`: _classify_transition OR 논리 적용
- `backtest_report.py`: TransitionTypeMetrics + 타입별 품질 섹션
- `abc_reversal_test.py`: A/B/C 실험 재현 스크립트

body:
> **Adding or updating a single faculty member?** Use our [self-service form](https://csrankings.org/submit/) instead — it's faster and validates your entry automatically!

## Required Checklist

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md) and check **all** boxes that apply.
Delete any lines that don't apply to your PR.

### Identity & Format
- [x] My GitHub profile shows my full name[^1]
- [x] PR title is descriptive (not "Update csrankings-x.csv")[^2]
- [x] One PR per institution, all changes combined[^3]
- [x] Only modified `csrankings-[a-z].csv` or `old/industry.csv`[^4]
- [x] Did NOT use Excel[^5]
- [x] No spaces after commas, no missing fields[^6]
- [x] Entries in alphabetical order by full name[^7]

### Data Accuracy
- [x] Name matches [DBLP](https://dblp.org) exactly (including 0001 suffixes)[^8]
- [x] Homepage URL works and shows name + affiliation[^9]
- [x] Google Scholar ID is the 12-character code only[^10]

### Eligibility
- [x] Faculty is full-time, tenure-track[^11]
- [x] Can **solely** advise CS PhD students[^12]
- [x] If not in CS department: included justification with links[^13]

### New Institutions
- [x] If adding new institution: opened issue first[^14]
- [x] Adding **all** CS faculty (not just one)[^15]

---

[^1]: Anonymous submissions are rejected to ensure accountability. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#non-anonymous)
[^2]: Generic titles make the PR queue difficult to manage. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-title)
[^3]: Multiple PRs for one institution create merge conflicts. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#one-pr)
[^4]: Other files are auto-generated or require maintainer access. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#allowed-files)
[^5]: Excel corrupts Google Scholar IDs by converting them to formulas. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-excel)
[^6]: Malformed CSV lines break the data pipeline. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#csv-format)
[^7]: Alphabetical order makes entries easy to find and reduces merge conflicts. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#alphabetical)
[^8]: Publications are matched by exact DBLP name; mismatches = zero papers counted. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#dblp-name)
[^9]: Automated validation fetches homepage to verify affiliation. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#homepage)
[^10]: Full URLs or `&hl=en` suffixes break the Scholar lookup. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#scholar-id)
[^11]: Adjuncts, visitors, and part-time faculty are excluded. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#tenure-track)
[^12]: Faculty who can only co-advise don't meet inclusion criteria. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#sole-advising)
[^13]: E.g., courtesy appointment in CS, or graduate program membership. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#non-cs-dept)
[^14]: Institution must be added to `institutions.csv` first by maintainer. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#new-institution)
[^15]: Partial departments skew rankings; all-or-nothing ensures fairness. [more info](https://github.com/emeryberger/CSrankings/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md#entire-dept)

body:
### Motivation
- Custom processes were shown as "reference only" and did not expose start/pause/cancel controls, causing the UI to differ from built-in processes.
- The circled help message was misleading because custom processes should be actionable once created.
- Make custom processes behave identically to built-ins at runtime so users can start, pause, cancel, and collect results.

### Description
- Added `getProcessDefinition` and changed game-state APIs (`startProcess`, `finishProcess`, `cancelProcess`, `finishProcessNow`, `hasRequiredAndConsumedItems`) to accept an optional `processDefinition` so handlers can operate on custom definitions passed at runtime.
- Updated `frontend/src/components/svelte/Process.svelte` to stop treating custom processes as read-only, remove the custom-only note, always render standard action controls, and pass the resolved `process` into game-state helpers via the new signatures.
- Simplified interval handling so the component consistently maintains runtime state updates for both built-in and custom processes.
- Updated tests to match the new behavior and signatures in `frontend/src/components/__tests__/Process.spec.ts` and `frontend/__tests__/ProcessCustom.test.js` (instant-finish assertion and custom-process control expectations).

### Testing
- Updated unit tests: `frontend/src/components/__tests__/Process.spec.ts` and `frontend/__tests__/ProcessCustom.test.js` were modified to assert the new behavior and function call signatures.
- Attempted to install frontend dependencies and start the dev server, but `npm install` failed with a dependency resolution error (`ERESOLVE`) preventing running the full test suite and dev server smoke tests.

body:
Adds comprehensive warm transfer functionality enabling AI-to-human agent handoffs via Twilio conference calls. Customers can request to speak with a human agent during calls, triggering automatic agent selection from a database-managed pool.

Core changes:
- New warm_transfer handler with automatic agent selection from support_numbers table
- Conference call orchestration with 4-stage flow: agent call → conference creation → agent join monitoring → customer transfer
- Database-driven agent pool (support_numbers table) with status tracking (AVAILABLE/BUSY/OFFLINE)
- Automatic resource cleanup via conference-end webhooks (agents + outbound numbers)
- Template example (trip_feedback_with_warm_transfer.json) with transfer_to_agent function

Technical implementation:
- TwilioConferenceService: multi-stage conference creation with polling & timeout handling
- Agent status atomically locked during transfers (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
- Conference callbacks track lifecycle for cleanup (conference_sid stored in agent record)
- Skip hangup during transfer (customer stays in conference when AI disconnects)
- Priority-based agent selection with fallback handling

New files:
- app/ai/voice/agents/breeze_buddy/handlers/internal/warm_transfer.py
- app/ai/voice/agents/breeze_buddy/services/telephony/twilio/conference.py
- app/database/migrations/011_create_support_numbers_table.sql
- app/database/accessor/breeze_buddy/support_numbers.py
- app/database/queries/breeze_buddy/support_numbers.py
- app/schemas/breeze_buddy/support_numbers.py
- docs/warm-transfer/TWILIO_WARM_TRANSFER_FLOW.md

- app/ai/voice/agents/breeze_buddy/examples/templates/trip_feedback_with_warm_transfer.json
- docs/AGENT_CONNECTION_FLOW.md
- .github/copilot-instructions.md

Modified files:
- Agent, handlers, template builder, context (add telephony_service access)
- Twilio/Exotel providers (add create_conference abstract method)
- Call manager (skip cleanup during warm transfer)
- Static config (warm transfer timeout/polling settings)
- Callback handlers (conference-status endpoint for cleanup)

Docs:
- Comprehensive warm transfer guide (README_WARM_TRANSFER.md)
- Twilio conference flow documentation
- Updated copilot instructions with project overview

body: ### Motivation - Reduce page load cost and bandwidth on public pages by using lazy, responsive images and low-data fallbacks. - Improve perceived performance and UX with skeleton loaders and smooth transitions. - Reduce database load for home and portfolio lists via short-lived caching with deterministic invalidation on content changes. - Surface quicker contact actions with floating WhatsApp/call buttons for better conversion. ### Description - Added 5-minute caching to the home and portfolio controllers and implemented cache keys/version bumps and invalidation in `Project`, `Category`, `Service`, and `Testimonial` models so updates flush relevant caches. - Implemented a low-data mode (cookie) and a toggle in the nav that serves thumbnails or defers video embeds until user interaction. - Converted several image outputs to responsive, lazy-loaded `` with `srcset`/`sizes`, added skeleton shimmer handling (`.media-frame.is-loading`) and small JavaScript to remove loaders on load and to inject videos on demand. - UI polish changes include smooth transition utilities and floating contact actions; modified files include controllers (`app/Http/Controllers/Public/HomeController.php`, `PortfolioController.php`), models (`app/Models/Project.php`, `Category.php`, `Service.php`, `Testimonial.php`), and view templates under `resources/views/public/` (`layout.blade.php`, `partials/nav.blade.php`, `home.blade.php`, `portfolio/index.blade.php`, `projects/show.blade.php`, `videos.blade.php`). ### Testing - No automated tests were executed during this rollout. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/tasks/task_e_6966033b557c832bb77aaaa16be52e49)

### Motivation
- Prevent valid report downloads from returning 404 when `settings.data_dir` is configured as a relative path.
- Ensure the download safety check correctly detects files under the `reports` folder even with relative `data_dir` values.
- Maintain the existing path traversal protection while addressing the false-negative caused by inconsistent path resolution.

### Description
- Resolve the `reports` directory with `Path(...).resolve()` before constructing `file_path` to ensure both sides of the check are absolute.
- Replace the parent containment check with `file_path.is_relative_to(reports_dir)` to robustly validate that the requested file lives inside the reports directory.
- Change applied in `app/main.py` within the `/reports/download/{filename}` handler.

author: amirbiron
body:
עשיתי תיקון שמסביר בדיוק את ההתנהגות שתיארת (“כפתורים לא מגיבים” + “אין לוגים”):

ה־JS של Web Push לא היה חסין: אם אחת מפונקציות האתחול האחרות בדף (initConfigRadar וכו׳) זורקת חריגה, כל הסקריפט יכול להיעצר לפני שמחברים click לכפתורים.
תיקנתי כך ש־Web Push מאותחל רק אחרי DOM-ready ובתוך try/catch, כדי ששום שגיאה אחרת לא תקטע אותו.
הוספתי type="button" לכפתורים (ליתר ביטחון) והוספתי סטטוס מיידי (“בודק תמיכה…/מכבה…/שולח…”) כדי שתראה שהקליק נקלט.
זה כבר commit+push לענף cursor/worker-push-delivery-url-ba24 (קומיט: d1709527).

אם אחרי הדיפלוי עדיין לא מגיב: תפתח DevTools בדפדפן ותבדוק אם יש warning בשם web push UI elements missing או settings init... failed — זה יגיד לנו בדיוק איפה נתקע.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Strengthens the Web Push section in `webapp/templates/settings.html` to avoid broken click handlers and improve UX.
> 
> - Defers initialization to DOM-ready and wraps `initSmoothScrollSettingsCard`, `initConfigRadar`, `initSharedThemesAdmin`, and new `initWebPushSettings` in try/catch to prevent a single failure from stopping others
> - Adds `initWebPushSettings` with a one-time guard, strict UI element presence checks, and clearer status updates for `enablePush`, `disablePush`, `testPush`, and `refreshPushUi`
> - Sets `type="button"` on `#pushEnableBtn`, `#pushDisableBtn`, `#pushTestBtn` to prevent unintended form submission
> - Improves user feedback with immediate status messages (e.g., "בודק תמיכה…/מכבה…/שולח…") and detailed error handling/logging
>

author: ajaysundark
body:
If there's a delete rule reconciliation, the finalizer triggers taint removal. This node update triggered node-reconciliation, which sometimes tried to re-add the taint when working with stale cache.

The patch here is that rule cache update should happen as the first step in `reconcileDelete` before `cleanupTaintsForRule`, so any further node reconciliation works with the latest update. 

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-readiness-controller/issues/83

author: mensfeld
body:
## Summary

Fixes flaky test `kill_all_no_containers` by improving the `kill` command to handle already-stopped and nonexistent containers gracefully.

## Problem

The `kill` command failed when encountering containers in unexpected states:
- Tried to stop already-stopped containers → error
- Treated nonexistent containers as "successfully killed" 
- Exit code 1 instead of expected 0 for cleanup operations

This caused the `kill_all_no_containers` test to be flaky when leftover containers (like `coi-build`) existed in stopped state.

## Solution

**Two improvements to `internal/cli/kill.go`:**

1. **Check container exists first** (before any operations)
   - Verify container exists using `mgr.Exists()`
   - Show warning and skip if not found
   - Prevents misleading "successfully killed" messages

2. **Skip stop for already-stopped containers**
   - Check if container is running with `mgr.Running()`
   - Only call `Stop()` if actually running
   - Prevents "already stopped" errors from Incus

## Testing

**New integration test:**
- `tests/kill/kill_stopped_container_gracefully.py`
- Launches container → stops it → kills stopped container
- Verifies kill succeeds without errors

**All 10 kill tests pass locally:**
```bash
$ pytest tests/kill/ -v
...
tests/kill/kill_no_args.py::test_kill_no_args PASSED
tests/kill/kill_running_container.py::test_kill_running_container PASSED
tests/kill/kill_force_flag.py::test_kill_with_force_flag PASSED
tests/kill/kill_multiple_containers.py::test_kill_multiple_containers PASSED
tests/kill/kill_nonexistent_container.py::test_kill_nonexistent_container PASSED
tests/kill/kill_idempotent.py::test_kill_idempotent PASSED
tests/kill/kill_all_no_containers.py::test_kill_all_no_containers PASSED
tests/kill/kill_stopped_container_gracefully.py::test_kill_stopped_container_gracefully PASSED
tests/kill/kill_all_with_force.py::test_kill_all_with_force PASSED
tests/kill/kill_stopped_container.py::test_kill_stopped_container PASSED

============================= 10 passed in 53.10s ==============================
```

**Fixed tests:**
- ✅ `kill_all_no_containers` (previously flaky - failed with leftover stopped containers)
- ✅ `kill_nonexistent_container` (previously failed - incorrectly reported success)
- ✅ `kill_stopped_container_gracefully` (new test)

## Files Changed

- `internal/cli/kill.go` - Added existence check and running state check before operations
- `tests/kill/kill_stopped_container_gracefully.py` - New integration test (85 lines)

## Benefits

- More robust handling of edge cases (stopped/nonexistent containers)
- Eliminates flaky test failures during cleanup operations
- Better error messages for users
- No breaking changes to existing behavior

author: pgolm
body:
Preserves llm_provider-* headers in error responses returned to clients. Previously, when an LLM provider returned an error (e.g., BadRequestError), any useful debugging headers from the provider's response were lost.

 ### Problem

When LiteLLM catches provider exceptions and re-raises them as typed exceptions (e.g., BadRequestError, ContentPolicyViolationError), the original response headers were being discarded. This meant clients couldn't access provider-specific debugging information that was included in error response headers.

### Solution

  1. **BadRequestError**: Now preserves headers from the original response when constructing the httpx.Response object
  2. **ContextWindowExceededError** / **ContentPolicyViolationError**: Pass through the original response to the parent class instead of creating a mock response without headers
  3. Proxy error handling: Extract **llm_provider-*** prefixed headers from exception responses and include them in the error response returned to clients

author: copilot
body:
Event system (EventPacket, Subscriber, EventData) deviates from component architecture patterns in type organization, FlatBuffers coupling, and conversion logic. This PR provides analysis and implementation roadmap.

## Documents Added

### EVENT_SYSTEM_ANALYSIS.md
Technical analysis comparing current event patterns vs established component patterns:
- **Type coupling**: Event types include FlatBuffers headers; components don't
- **Schema naming**: Mixed `Data`/`Fbs`/none suffixes vs consistent component patterns  
- **Conversion logic**: Scattered across 3 factories vs centralized configurators
- **Cross-schema deps**: Entity schemas embed event schemas vs loose coupling

### EVENT_SYSTEM_COMPARISON.md
Visual architecture comparison with ASCII diagrams:
```
Component Pattern (established):
Runtime Type → Conversion Layer → FlatBuffers Schema
     ↓              ↓                    ↓
 No includes    Configurator      Serialization only

Event Pattern (current):
Runtime Type ←includes← FlatBuffers Schema
     ↓
Coupled to serialization format
```

### EVENT_SYSTEM_REFACTORING_PLAN.md
6-phase implementation plan (11-17 hours):
1. **Decouple runtime types** - Extract `EventType.h`, add conversion layer
2. **Standardize naming** - `EventDataData` → `EventDataUnion`, `SubscriberFbs` → `SubscriberData`
3. **Reduce coupling** - Create `event_reference.fbs` with lightweight refs
4. **Consolidate logic** - Create `FlatbuffersEventConfigurator`
5. **Testing** - Conversion tests, integration validation
6. **Documentation** - Migration guide, cleanup

### EVENT_SYSTEM_QUICK_START.md
Implementation checklist with code patterns and validation commands.

## Core Issues

**Before (current):**
```cpp
// EventPacket.h
#include "events_generated.h"  // FlatBuffers coupling

struct EventPacket {
    EventType event_type;  // FlatBuffers enum
};
```

**After (proposed):**
```cpp
// EventPacket.h
#include "EventType.h"  // Independent enum

struct EventPacket {
    EventType event_type;  // Runtime enum
};

// event_type_conversion.cpp
EventType ConvertFromFlatBuffers(EventTypeFbs fbs_type);
```

## Recommendations Summary

- Separate runtime enums from FlatBuffers schemas
- Standardize schema naming: tables use `TypeNameData`, unions use `TypeNameUnion`
- Replace embedded event data in entity schemas with lightweight references
- Consolidate conversion logic following `FlatbuffersEntityConfigurator` pattern

Documentation provides complete implementation plan with code examples, testing strategies, and rollback procedures.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure password reset requests return `email_not_found` when the email is not in Supabase instead of a generic failure message.
- Provide a complete recovery flow so the recovery link opens a UI to set and confirm a new password and updates Supabase.
- Inject the Supabase recovery link into the Brevo template so the user receives a working reset link.
- Improve front-end error handling to surface clear messages for not-found and Brevo/Supabase failures.

### Description
- Added `sendPasswordResetEmail` in `cloudflare-worker.js` that verifies the email via Supabase admin `users` endpoint, returns `email_not_found` for missing users, calls `generateRecoveryLink`, and includes `RECOVERY_LINK` in the Brevo `templateId` params.
- Changed `generateRecoveryLink` to return an object `{ link, status }` (and error text on failures) so callers can surface 400/404 as `email_not_found` and otherwise report generation errors.
- Updated `index.html` to add a `Forgot password?` button, a hidden `#resetPasswordFields` block, `handlePasswordResetRequest`, and `handleSetNewPassword` which uses `supabaseClient.auth.updateUser` to apply the new password.
- Updated redirect handling in `handleVerificationRedirect` and `setAuthMode` to detect the Supabase recovery flow, set the client session from URL tokens, show the set-password form, and adjust button/text/UI state; also improved unsubscribe/error detection to look for `email_not_found`.

### Testing
- Started a local static server with `python -m http.server` to serve `index.html`, which launched successfully.
- Attempted a Playwright script to open the modal and capture a screenshot, but the Playwright run timed out and did not complete (failed).
- No automated unit or integration tests were added or executed beyond the above browser check attempt.
- Worker-side integration (Supabase/Brevo) was not executed in CI; runtime behavior was implemented to return clear status codes for downstream handling.

### Motivation

- Provide guidance for handling type-checker warnings in `SQLModel`/`SQLAlchemy` code without resorting to unsafe ORM rewrites.
- Capture project conventions that favor runtime correctness and explicitly allow targeted type-ignore and optional typing on columns.
- Preserve correct SQL expression usage by discouraging string-based replacements for methods like `like`, `desc`, and `is_`.
- Make this guidance discoverable from the existing integration docs.

### Description

- Add `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` containing the requested type-checking/ORM rules: `prefer runtime correctness`, `don’t rewrite ORM for type checker`, `allow # type: ignore[attr-defined]`, `optional ColumnElement annotations`, and `never replace like/desc/is_ with string logic`.
- Update `docs/INTEGRATION.md` to add a link to `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` so the guidance is easy to find.
- Modified files: added `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` and updated `docs/INTEGRATION.md` to reference it.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run because this is a docs-only change.
- No code paths were modified, so CI and unit tests should be unaffected by this change.

author: futuroptimist
body:
### Motivation
- Custom processes were rendered as “reference only” and lacked the standard start/pause/cancel/collect controls, making the UI inconsistent with built-in processes.
- The game state handlers assumed only built-in catalog entries, preventing custom process definitions from being started or managed correctly.

### Description
- Updated `Process.svelte` to remove the custom-only guard so custom processes render the same action buttons as built-ins and to pass the active `process` definition into action calls (e.g. `startProcess(processId, process)`).
- Enhanced `frontend/src/utils/gameState/processes.js` to resolve a process definition from (in order) a passed `processDefinition`, the built-in catalog, or the stored `gameState` entry, and to accept an optional `processDefinition` parameter on actions so custom definitions are honored and persisted with the running process.
- Made defensive changes to handle missing arrays (use `?? []`) when burning/adding items and when checking requirements.
- Updated unit/component tests (`Process.spec.ts`, `ProcessCustom.test.js`) to expect standard controls for custom processes and to verify the action functions receive the process definition.

### Testing
- Installed dependencies with `npm ci` which completed successfully.
- Ran `npm run lint` which failed in this environment due to a missing `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` dependency in the frontend toolchain.
- Attempted `npm run test:ci` (via `node run-tests.js`) but the run was interrupted/stalled and did not complete in this environment.
- Updated and added component unit tests; these tests were modified to assert the new behavior but full CI test suite was not completed locally due to the lint/test environment issues described above.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
⚡ **Performance Improvement**

This PR optimizes the `BallFlightSimulator` in `shared/python/ball_flight_physics.py`.

**What changed:**
- Refactored `_equations_of_motion` to perform physics calculations directly using NumPy arrays instead of constructing intermediate dictionaries.
- Precomputed constant values (gravity vector, drag/lift constant terms) to avoid re-calculation in the integration loop.
- Optimized vector norm calculations.

**Why:**
- The previous implementation created a dictionary of forces and a list of arrays at every time step of the RK45 solver, causing significant allocation overhead.
- Profiling indicated this was a hot path for trajectory simulation.

**Impact:**
- Reduces simulation time for a standard driver shot.
- Improves responsiveness when running batch simulations or Monte Carlo analyses.

**Verification:**
- Validated with `tests/unit/test_ball_flight_physics.py` (all tests passed).
- Benchmarked simulation loop (consistent performance observed).

(다른 페이지/기능 깨짐 여부) - [x] API, DB 변경 시 문서화했습니다. - [x] 새로운 의존성 추가 시 팀과 공유했습니다. ## 테스트 및 검증 내용 > 어떻게 테스트했고, 어떤 결과를 확인했는지 적어주세요. 소켓 명세에 맞게 mock 데이터를 구성한 뒤, 라운드 종료 페이지에서 각 플레이어의 리플레이가 정상적으로 재생되는 것을 확인했습니다. ## 추가 참고 사항 > 리뷰어가 알아야 할 특이사항, 주의사항 등을 적어주세요. ### 같이 논의하고 싶은 부분 - 서비스 전반에서 **영어 / 한글 사용을 통일할 필요**가 있어보입니다! 우선 이번 라운드 결과 페이지는 한글 기준으로 맞춰두었습니다. - 리플레이도 왼쪽 상단에 그려지는 현상이 있는데 캔버스 픽셀/좌표 처리와 관련된 문제로 보여요.. 알아보고 있숨다! ## 스크린샷 / UI 변경 (선택) > UI가 변경된 경우 스크린샷을 첨부해주세요. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * 라운드 종료 화면에 플레이어 재생 섹션과 프롬프트 재생 섹션 추가 * 플레이어 재생 카드에 랭크 배지, 유사도(%) 및 스트로크 기반 재생 표시 * **Chores / Refactor** * 일부 기존 재생/참조 카드 제거로 레이아웃 단순화 및 전체 레이아웃 조정 * 라운드 결과 데이터에 score 및 ranking 필드 추가 * **Tests** * 캔버스 스케일링·좌표 변환 로직에 대한 단위 테스트 추가 ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

author: totto
body:
## Summary

Add comprehensive skill documentation for 35 manufacturer handlers that were missing skill files. This brings total manufacturer skills from **51 to 86**, achieving comprehensive coverage for all handlers in the library.

## Skills Added

### Batch 1 (10 skills)
- **AMS** - ams-OSRAM sensors, LEDs, optical components
- **AllianceMemory** - SRAM, DRAM, Flash memory
- **CirrusLogic** - Audio codecs, amplifiers, ADCs/DACs
- **Coilcraft** - Inductors, transformers, RF components
- **Everlight** - LEDs, optocouplers, photodetectors
- **FTDI** - USB interface ICs, bridge chips
- **GigaDevice** - Flash memory, MCUs, sensors
- **Harting** - Industrial connectors, Han series
- **Honeywell** - Pressure/humidity/magnetic sensors
- **MPS** - DC-DC converters, LED drivers, motor drivers

### Batch 2 (10 skills)
- **Macronix** - NOR Flash, NAND Flash, ROM
- **PhoenixContact** - Terminal blocks, connectors
- **PowerIntegrations** - AC-DC converters, LED drivers
- **PulseElectronics** - Transformers, inductors, magnetics
- **Realtek** - Audio codecs, Ethernet controllers
- **Sensirion** - Environmental sensors (humidity, gas, particulate)
- **SeoulSemi** - LEDs, SunLike LEDs
- **SiTime** - MEMS oscillators, timing solutions
- **Sumida** - Inductors, transformers, coils
- **Vicor** - Power modules, DC-DC converters

### Batch 3 (10 skills)
- **AKM** - Audio DACs/ADCs, magnetic sensors
- **Abracon** - Crystals, oscillators, antennas
- **Cree** - High-power LEDs, XLamp series
- **DiodesInc** - Discrete semiconductors, logic ICs
- **Epson** - Crystals, oscillators, RTC modules
- **Fairchild** - MOSFETs, transistors (now ON Semi)
- **IQD** - Frequency control products, TCXOs
- **LG** - LEDs, camera modules
- **LogicIC** - 74xx/CD4xxx series logic ICs
- **Lumileds** - LUXEON LEDs, automotive LEDs

### Batch 4 (5 skills)
- **NDK** - Crystals, oscillators, timing devices
- **Nexteria** - Nexperia discrete semiconductors
- **OSRAM** - LEDs, optocouplers, automotive lighting
- **Qualcomm** - Mobile SoCs, WiFi/BT, RF front-end
- **Spansion** - Flash memory, MCUs (now Infineon)

## Each Skill Includes
- Manufacturer overview and product categories
- MPN pattern structure and decoding examples
- Supported ComponentTypes from the handler
- Package code and series extraction rules
- Real-world example MPNs with explanations
- Handler implementation notes
- Learnings and quirks section

## Test Plan
- [x] Skills are documentation only - no code changes
- [x] Verified all 35 skill files created in `.claude/skills/manufacturers/`
- [x] Each skill follows the established format from existing skills

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

author: houssamcherhabil
body:
Bug: In nextLoginStep(), onboarding was unconditionally marked as complete for ALL users on login, preventing new users from ever seeing the onboarding carousel.

Fix: Only skip onboarding if localStorage already has 'fixair_onboarding_done' set (meaning user previously completed it). New users will now see the onboarding carousel as intended.

body:
### Motivation
- The light theme header visually blended into the page and needed a clear but non-aggressive separation from content.
- Keep the dark theme unchanged while improving readability and depth for light mode.
- Use only theme CSS variables to control visual differences and avoid any JS logic changes.

### Description
- Added and adjusted theme variables in `css/styles.css` including `--header-bg`, `--header-border-color`, `--header-shadow`, `--nav-tab-bg`, `--nav-tab-active-bg`, and `--user-popover-shadow` (with `:root[data-theme="light"]` overrides).
- Applied these variables to the header container using `.app-header { background: var(--header-bg); box-shadow: var(--header-shadow); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--header-border-color); }` to create a readable layer in light theme.
- Increased contrast for navigation tabs by setting ` .app-nav .btn.toggle { background: var(--nav-tab-bg); }` and ` .app-nav .btn.toggle.active { background: var(--nav-tab-active-bg); }` for light theme only via variables.
- Gave the user popover a subtle elevation in light mode by using `box-shadow: var(--user-popover-shadow)` on `.user-popover`.

### Testing
- Attempted a visual smoke test by launching a local server and running a Playwright script to capture a light-theme screenshot, but the browser process crashed (SIGSEGV/TargetClosedError) so the screenshot step failed.
- No unit test suite exists in the repo, so no unit tests were executed.
- The change is CSS-only and limited to `css/styles.css`, and the commit was created as `style(header): improve contrast and separation in light theme`.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
## 🚨 Severity: HIGH

### 💡 Vulnerability
The `generate_story` method in `BachataSyncEngine` accepted a raw string for `output_path`, allowing malicious users to potentially overwrite arbitrary files on the system (Path Traversal) or generate files with dangerous extensions (e.g., `.sh`).

### 🔧 Fix Implementation (SOLID)
* **Encapsulation:** Created `StoryGenerationInput` Pydantic model to encapsulate validation logic.
* **Constraint:** Enforced strict rules:
    * Must end with `.mp4`.
    * Must not contain `..` (directory traversal).
    * Filename must match `^[\w\-. ]+$` (safe characters only).
* **Type Safety:** Used Pydantic for robust type checking and validation before file operations.

### ✅ Verification
Added `tests/test_security_verification.py`. Confirmed that:
* Attempting `../file.mp4` raises `ValidationError`.
* Attempting `script.sh` raises `ValidationError`.
* Valid `output.mp4` works correctly.

author: calistaverner
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure a FULL world reset on hot-reload (F5) so no entity shadows / stale render state remain.
- Make ECS the single authoritative registry for entity bindings and remove local duplicate maps.
- Clear render-side caches (post/tonemap and shadow maps) when the world is reset to avoid visual artifacts.
- Remove legacy/compat ctors in API modules to enforce the new module lifecycle contract.

### Description
- Added `EngineApiImpl.__resetWorldState(String)` which resets the ECS, calls `physics.__clearAll()` and triggers render cache reset.  
- Added `RenderApiImpl.__resetWorldCache(String)` to clear lighting caches and call `PostModule.resetCache()` and `ShadowModule.clearShadowMaps(...)` on the JME thread.  
- Wired the world hot-reload path to call `__resetWorldState(...)` from `KWorld.hotReload(...)` so F5 performs a full engine/world state reset.  
- Reworked `SurfaceRegistry` to stop using local surface<->entity maps and instead query the ECS `Surface` component for bindings, and added `PostModule.resetCache()` plus removed legacy constructors from `DebugDrawApiImpl` and `HudApiImpl`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.
- Changes were committed after local edits and basic compilation/inspection in the working tree (no CI run requested).

## Description:
This PR fixes an issue in the generated SCSS tokens where token names containing dots (e.g. 0.5) could cause Sass compilation errors.
The fix ensures that token names are escaped in both:
 - the generated SCSS variable name
 - the corresponding var() reference
This makes the generated SCSS compatible with Sass consumers.

Bug repported in support channel: [Teams Post](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/message/19:d6c35634a3d04095a2e59ad0d9951c50@thread.tacv2/1768292808275?tenantId=2eb07b91-f9f8-437b-a89e-59f55e565c11&groupId=cec93f98-ceee-42bd-bfde-a6b51fc1194e&parentMessageId=1768292808275&teamName=Solid%20Design%20System%20Community%20(Team)&channelName=SDS-Support&createdTime=1768292808275)

author: finxo
body:
# Pull Request

## 📝 Summary
This pull request introduces a complete overhaul of the workflow management interface by implementing a modern, interactive Text User Interface (TUI) using the Textual framework. The new "Workflows" screen replaces the previous static list with a dynamic, two-panel layout. This design significantly improves user experience by allowing users to easily filter and browse available workflows based on their source plugin.

## 🔧 Changes Made
- **New Workflow Screen**: Implemented a new `WorkflowsScreen` with a two-panel layout:
    - A left panel lists all source plugins (plus an "All" filter) to categorize workflows.
    - A right panel displays the list of workflows, which dynamically updates when a plugin is selected.
- **TUI Architecture Refactor**:
    - Introduced a `BaseScreen` class to standardize screen structure, centralizing the status bar and a new global `HeaderWidget`.
    - The `HeaderWidget` provides a consistent title and back navigation experience across all screens.
    - Implemented a Dracula-based theme (`TITAN_THEME_CSS`) for a cohesive and polished visual identity.
- **Enhanced Interactivity**:
    - Added intuitive keyboard navigation using `left`/`right` arrows and `Tab` to switch focus between the plugin and workflow panels.
    - Standardized `escape` and `q` for back navigation, handled by the `BaseScreen`.
- **Developer Tooling**: Added a new preview command (`titan preview workflows`) and a corresponding preview application to allow for isolated development and testing of the `WorkflowsScreen` component.

## 🧪 Testing
- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] All tests passing

A standalone preview application (`workflows_preview.py`) was created to test the new screen's layout, filtering logic, and responsiveness in isolation with mocked data. All new UI components and interactions were manually validated.

### Motivation

- Close the verification gap in AS‑IS docs by treating `verify_all.cmd` + runtime snapshot as authoritative evidence and removing stale `NOT VERIFIED` markers.
- Make `SKIP` semantics explicit so smoke scripts that skip due to empty data (e.g. no invoices) are treated as PASS in readiness assessments.
- Ensure runbook and evidence index point to the actual repo scripts used for verification and token retrieval (so artifacts and commands match the code).
- Provide a single, discoverable runtime snapshot that references the commit and shows `verify_all PASS` for Stage 0 closure.

### Description

- Added `VERIFIED_BY_RUNTIME` status and `SKIP ≠ FAIL` guidance in `docs/as-is/NEFT_PLATFORM_READINESS_MAP.md` and marked Stage 0 as `CLOSED / VERIFIED` with runtime evidence via `docs/as-is/STATUS_SNAPSHOT_RUNTIME_LATEST.md`.
- Created `docs/as-is/STATUS_SNAPSHOT_RUNTIME_LATEST.md` (copied from `STATUS_SNAPSHOT_RUNTIME_2026-01-13.md`) and updated `docs/as-is/STATUS_SNAPSHOT_LATEST.md` to list canonical health/metrics endpoints and the pytest subset used by `verify_all.cmd`.
- Updated `docs/as-is/VERIFY_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md` to include `scripts/verify_all.cmd`, `scripts/get_admin_token.cmd`, and the smoke suite entries with explicit notes that `billing_smoke` and invoice state machine can return SKIP (OK).
- Expanded `docs/as-is/RUNBOOK_LOCAL.md`, `docs/as-is/NEFT_PLATFORM_AS_IS_MASTER.md`, and `docs/as-is/DB_SCHEMA_MAP.md` to reference the runtime snapshot and mark migrations/health endpoints as `VERIFIED_BY_RUNTIME` and to document `scripts/verify_all.cmd` and `scripts/get_admin_token.cmd` usage.

body:
# feat: Add Section 6 - Stray Pose Classifier (Weak Supervision)

## 📝 Description
[cite_start]This PR introduces **Section 6: Stray Pose Classifier**, which documents the primary **original contribution** of this work[cite: 1]. [cite_start]It details the methodology for classifying dog behaviors using a **Weak Supervision** approach, bypassing the need for expensive and subjective manual annotations[cite: 2].

## 🚀 Key Changes

### 1. Weak Supervision Methodology
* [cite_start]**Concept:** Labels are derived automatically from the dataset origin rather than manual tagging[cite: 4].
* **Label Assignment:**
    * [cite_start]`FYP Dataset` (Stray dogs) $\rightarrow$ **Label 1** (Stray)[cite: 4].
    * [cite_start]`Stanford Dogs` & `Dog's Skin Diseases` (Owned dogs) $\rightarrow$ **Label 0** (Owned)[cite: 4, 7].
* [cite_start]**Rationale:** Solves issues related to subjectivity, cost, inconsistency, and scalability in manual annotation[cite: 5].

### 2. Model Architecture (StrayPoseMLP)
* [cite_start]**Type:** Lightweight Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) designed for structured numeric input[cite: 9].
* [cite_start]**Input:** 72 features consisting of 24 normalized keypoints $(x, y, v)$[cite: 10].
* **Structure:** * Linear layers $(128, 64)$ with ReLU activation.
    * [cite_start]Batch Normalization and Dropout $(0.3)$ for regularization[cite: 11].
    * [cite_start]Final Sigmoid activation for binary classification[cite: 12].
* [cite_start]**Complexity:** Approximately **17,665 parameters**[cite: 13].

### 3. Behavioral Analysis
* [cite_start]The model implicitly captures postural patterns associated with stress or abandonment[cite: 14]:
    * *Tail position:* Tail tucked between legs (tail_start, tail_end).
    * *Head posture:* Low head/chin vs withers.
    * *Ear position:* Flattened ears.
    * *Stance:* Defensive crouching or asymmetry.

### 4. Training Configuration
* [cite_start]**Optimizer:** Adam ($lr=10^{-3}$)[cite: 15].
* **Loss Function:** BCELoss.
* [cite_start]**Epochs:** 100 (with Early Stopping at 15 epochs)[cite: 15].
* [cite_start]**Dataset:** Balanced split (Train 70% / Val 15% / Test 15%)[cite: 8].

## 📊 Motivation
Classifying "stray-like" vs "owned-like" posture is subjective. [cite_start]By assuming that dogs in the FYP dataset (street dogs) generally exhibit different body language compared to show dogs (Stanford), we can train a classifier using the source as a proxy label[cite: 6]. This allows for a reproducible and scalable pipeline.`

author: mozzius
body:
## Summary

Implements composer drafts with server-side storage and local media caching.

- Draft metadata stored on server via `app.bsky.draft.*` API endpoints
- Media files (images, videos) cached locally (filesystem on native, IndexedDB on web)
- "Drafts" button in composer top bar to access saved drafts
- Save/discard prompt when closing composer with unsaved changes
- Full support for restoring: text, facets, images, videos, GIFs, labels, threadgate/postgate settings

## Architecture

```
src/view/com/composer/drafts/
├── state/
│   ├── schema.ts         # Type definitions for draft display
│   ├── api.ts            # Serialization between ComposerState and server Draft
│   ├── queries.ts        # React Query hooks for CRUD operations
│   ├── storage.ts        # Native media storage (expo-file-system)
│   ├── storage.web.ts    # Web media storage (IndexedDB)
│   └── logger.ts         # Drafts-specific logger
├── DraftsButton.tsx      # "Drafts" button for composer top bar
├── DraftsListDialog.tsx  # Dialog listing all drafts
└── DraftItem.tsx         # Single draft row with preview
```

## How It Works

1. **Saving**: Composer state is serialized to server draft format. Media files are copied to local storage with a unique `localRef.path` key that's stored in the server draft.

2. **Loading**: Draft metadata is fetched from server. Media files are loaded from local storage using the `localRef.path` keys. Missing media (saved on another device) is indicated in the UI.

3. **Deleting**: Local media files are cleaned up, then the server draft is deleted.

## What's Supported

- ✅ Text with facets (mentions, links, tags)
- ✅ Images with alt text
- ✅ Videos with alt text  
- ✅ GIFs (Tenor) with alt text
- ✅ Labels (content warnings)
- ✅ Quote posts
- ✅ External link embeds
- ✅ Threadgate settings
- ✅ Postgate (embedding rules)
- ✅ Multi-post threads
- ✅ Dirty tracking (only prompt to save if changes made)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Create post with text + image, close composer, save draft
- [ ] Open drafts, verify preview shows correctly
- [ ] Load draft, verify content restores correctly
- [ ] Edit draft, save changes, verify updates
- [ ] Delete draft, verify removed from list
- [ ] Test GIF drafts restore correctly
- [ ] Test on web (IndexedDB storage)
- [ ] Test on iOS/Android (filesystem storage)
- [ ] Test draft with media saved on another device shows "missing media" indicator

author: jah0x
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent Alembic from running with an async driver URL while the runtime app uses an async driver, which can cause migrations to silently not apply.
- Fail fast when public migrations did not create essential tables to avoid mysterious runtime errors during seeding.
- Prevent seed logic from running against an empty `public` schema so bootstrap does not proceed on the wrong database or URL.

### Description
- Add `make_sync_database_url` and use it in `_alembic_config` so Alembic always receives a sync URL via `sqlalchemy.url` (file: `backend/app/services/migrations.py`).
- Replace the previous URL conversion with `make_sync_database_url` and keep `_sync_database_url()` delegating to it (file: `backend/app/services/migrations.py`).
- Add `verify_public_migrations` async function that checks `public.alembic_version` and `public.modules` exist and raises a `RuntimeError` if they are missing (file: `backend/app/services/migrations.py`).
- Invoke `verify_public_migrations(engine)` after `run_public_migrations` in both the bootstrap flow and the CLI `migrate_all` flow, and add a pre-seed check to abort seeding when `public` is empty (files: `backend/app/services/bootstrap.py`, `backend/app/cli.py`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

author: robinskil
body:
Fixes #153 

This pull request adds comprehensive new documentation for the Beacon Data Lake project, focusing on file formats, configuration, CLI tools, and advanced data management features. The key changes include detailed guides for the Beacon Binary Format, environment-based configuration, data table management (including logical and preset tables), dataset harmonization, and a new CLI tool overview. Additionally, a minor change was made to the GitHub Actions workflow.

**Documentation Additions and Improvements**

*Beacon Binary Format:*
- Added an overview of the Beacon Binary Format, including its open-source status, performance characteristics, compression support, and cloud storage integration.
- Provided a practical guide on using the Beacon Binary Format, including installation instructions, supported file formats, and command-line usage examples for creating, inspecting, and managing `.bbf` files.

*Configuration and Setup:*
- Introduced a new configuration guide detailing all environment variables available for customizing Beacon's behavior, including general, S3, NetCDF, and multiplexer settings.

*Data Lake Management:*
- Added documentation on managing data tables (collections), including examples for logical tables across various file formats (Zarr, NetCDF, Parquet, CSV, Arrow, BBF) and preset tables for advanced data product creation.
- Documented the dataset harmonization (schema merging) feature, explaining how Beacon unifies schemas from multiple datasets and handles n-dimensional data.

*CLI Tool:*
- Introduced documentation for the Beacon Data Lake CLI Tool, including installation steps, usage, and links to the CLI and Python SDK repositories.

**Workflow Update**

*CI/CD:*
- Simplified the GitHub Actions workflow for Pages deployment by removing the scheduled trigger and clarifying manual workflow dispatch.

author: sdilauro
body:
Closes #1031 

## Problem

Emojis and accented characters were showing as symbols in iOS local notifications, making notifications difficult to read and unprofessional.

## Solution

Added a flexible sanitization system that allows preserving or removing emojis and normalizing accented characters based on platform needs. By default, both emojis and accents are preserved to maintain message quality, but can be sanitized if display issues occur.

## Changes

### 1. New utility function: `NotificationUtils.sanitize_notification_text()`

**File:** `godot/src/notifications/notification_utils.gd`

- Added a new static function to sanitize notification text
- Parameters:
  - `text: String` - The text to sanitize
  - `remove_emojis: bool = false` - If true, removes emojis from the text
  - `normalize_accents: bool = false` - If true, normalizes accented characters (á→a, é→e, etc.)
- By default, preserves both emojis and accents
- Supports comprehensive emoji range detection (emoticons, symbols, pictographs, etc.)
- Supports normalization of common accented characters (Spanish, French, German, etc.)

### 2. Updated notification wrapper to use sanitization

**File:** `godot/src/notifications/local_os_wrapper.gd`

- Modified `schedule()` method to sanitize notification text before sending to native plugins
- Currently configured to preserve both emojis and accents (`remove_emojis=false`, `normalize_accents=false`)
- Can be easily adjusted if display issues are detected on specific devices

### 3. Added test button in Settings

**Files:** 
- `godot/src/ui/components/settings/settings.tscn`
- `godot/src/ui/components/settings/settings.gd`

- Added a test notification button in the Advanced/Dev Tools section
- Button: "Test Notification with Emojis"
- Schedules a test notification with emojis and accented characters after 5 seconds
- Useful for testing notification display on iOS devices


## Technical Details

### Emoji Detection

The function detects emojis across multiple Unicode ranges:
- Emoticons (U+1F600 to U+1F64F)
- Miscellaneous Symbols and Pictographs (U+1F300 to U+1F9FF)
- Transport and Map Symbols (U+1F680 to U+1F6FF)
- Supplemental Symbols and Pictographs (U+1F900 to U+1F9FF)
- Symbols and Pictographs Extended-A (U+1FA00 to U+1FAFF)
- And other emoji-related ranges

### Accent Normalization

Supports normalization for:
- Spanish: á, é, í, ó, ú, ñ, etc.
- French: à, è, ù, ç, etc.
- German: ä, ö, ü, ß, etc.
- And many other accented characters

## Files Modified

- `godot/src/notifications/notification_utils.gd` - Added sanitization function
- `godot/src/notifications/local_os_wrapper.gd` - Applied sanitization to notifications
- `godot/src/ui/components/settings/settings.tscn` - Added test button UI
- `godot/src/ui/components/settings/settings.gd` - Added test button handler

## Notes

- The sanitization is applied transparently to all local notifications
- No changes required in existing notification code
- The test button is only visible in Dev Tools section (non-production builds)
- iOS plugin already attempts to preserve emojis with UTF-8 encoding, but sanitization provides a fallback if encoding issues occur


## Testing

### Manual Testing

1. Open Settings → Dev Tools
2. Scroll to "Test Notification" section
3. Press "Test Notification with Emojis"
4. Wait 5 seconds and check the notification on the device
5. Verify:
   - Emojis display correctly (🎉 🚀)
   - Accented characters display correctly (áéíóú ÁÉÍÓÚ ñ Ñ)

### Expected Behavior

**Default (current):**
- Title: "🎉 Notificación de Prueba 🎉"
- Body: "Esta es una notificación de prueba con emojis 🚀 y acentos: áéíóú ÁÉÍÓÚ ñ Ñ"
- Both emojis and accents should be preserved

- Fix overview backdrop blur produced solid gray workspaces and edge artifacts because background-layer surfaces were not always included when producing the blur texture and the blur sampling was fixed and not configurable.
New 
- Provide a user-configurable sampling quality to trade off smoothness vs cost while keeping the blur radius driven by the existing `backdrop_blur` and overview animation progress.

### Description
- Add a new config option `backdrop_blur_quality` on `Overview` with a default of `2.0` and knuffel parsing in `niri-config` (fields and merge logic updated). 
- Update the fragment shader `overview_blur.frag` to accept a `blur_quality` uniform and sample a configurable kernel based on that value for 1–3 quality levels.

- Document `backdrop-blur-quality` in `docs/wiki/Configuration:-Miscellaneous.md` and `docs/wiki/Overview.md` and add the render element to the `niri_render_elements!` list.

## Summary
We have added a defconfig configuration to set the page size of the flash. According to the CFI protocol, the flash supports a single write operation with a data volume ranging from byte size up to the maximum number of bytes. However, the MTD device structure requires defining a page size, which serves as the minimum write unit of the flash. Hence, this configuration is introduced. Any page size within the range of 1 to the maximum number of bytes is considered valid.

## Impact
Only impacts CFI-Flash writes

We have completed the validation based on the QEMU environment.

author: matt-riley
body:
## Summary

This PR implements dual-mode authentication support for the mjr.wtf URL shortener, enabling the server to run in either standard HTTP mode (Bearer/Session authentication) or Tailscale mode (WhoIs-based network authentication).

## Related Issues

- Closes mjrwtf-ycu.5: Update Server Initialization for Dual-Mode Support
- Closes mjrwtf-ycu.6: Update HTTP Server for Conditional Route Protection
- Closes mjrwtf-ycu.7: Update Page Handlers for Tailscale User Context
- Closes mjrwtf-ycu.8: Add Integration Tests for Tailscale Mode

## Changes

### Server Infrastructure (`internal/infrastructure/http/server/server.go`)

**Why:** The server needed to support two authentication modes without code changes - just configuration via `TAILSCALE_ENABLED`.

**How:**
- Added `tailscaleClient` field to `Server` struct to store the WhoIs client
- Introduced `ServerOption` functional option pattern with `WithTailscaleClient()` for clean dependency injection
- Updated `New()` to accept variadic options: `func New(cfg *config.Config, db *sql.DB, logger zerolog.Logger, opts ...ServerOption) (*Server, error)`
- Added logging to indicate which authentication mode is active on startup

### Conditional Route Protection

**Why:** Admin routes (`/dashboard`, `/api/*`) need different authentication based on mode:
- Tailscale mode: Network membership IS the authentication (WhoIs lookup)
- Standard mode: Bearer tokens or session cookies

**How:**
- Updated `setupPageRoutes()` to conditionally apply:
  - Tailscale mode: `middleware.TailscaleAuth()` for `/dashboard`
  - Standard mode: `middleware.RequireSession()` with redirect to `/login`
- Updated `setupAPIRoutes()` to conditionally apply:
  - Tailscale mode: `middleware.TailscaleAuth()` for `/api/*`
  - Standard mode: `middleware.SessionOrBearerAuth()` for `/api/*`
- Login/logout routes are hidden in Tailscale mode (network membership replaces login)

### Page Handler Updates (`internal/infrastructure/http/handlers/page_handler.go`)

**Why:** The Dashboard handler needed to work with both authentication modes.

**How:**
- Updated `Dashboard()` to check both `middleware.GetUserID()` (Tailscale) and `middleware.GetSessionUserID()` (Session) for user identity
- Tailscale auth sets `UserIDKey` context, Session auth sets `SessionUserIDKey` context
- Handler now gracefully falls back between the two

### Main Entry Point (`cmd/server/main.go`)

**Why:** Server initialization needed to create and manage Tailscale server lifecycle.

**How:**
- Added conditional Tailscale server creation when `cfg.TailscaleEnabled == true`
- Creates `TailscaleServer` and `WhoIsClient` instances
- Passes client to server via `WithTailscaleClient()` option
- Added Tailscale server shutdown in graceful termination path

### Integration Tests (`internal/infrastructure/http/server/tailscale_integration_test.go`)

Comprehensive test coverage including:
- Public routes accessible without auth in both modes
- Admin routes require valid Tailscale authentication
- Standard mode fallback to Bearer/Session auth
- WhoIs failure returns 401
- Login/logout routes hidden in Tailscale mode
- User identity propagation to handlers
- Metrics endpoint behavior is unaffected by mode
- Both modes can coexist in the same codebase

## Test Coverage

All tests pass:
```
go test ./... ✓
```

Key test files:
- `tailscale_test.go` - Unit tests for server options and mode switching
- `tailscale_integration_test.go` - End-to-end integration tests

## Backward Compatibility

✅ **100% backward compatible** - existing deployments work unchanged:
- `TAILSCALE_ENABLED=false` (default) uses existing Bearer token and session authentication
- All existing API clients continue to work
- No database changes required
- No breaking changes to configuration

## Usage

### Standard Mode (default)
```bash
export TAILSCALE_ENABLED=false
export AUTH_TOKEN=your-secret-token
./server
```

### Tailscale Mode
```bash
export TAILSCALE_ENABLED=true
export TAILSCALE_HOSTNAME=mjr-wtf
export TAILSCALE_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/tailscale
# AUTH_TOKEN still needed for metrics auth if METRICS_AUTH_ENABLED=true
./server
```

## Dependencies

This PR builds on:
- PR for mjrwtf-ycu.3 (Tailscale server wrapper)
- PR for mjrwtf-ycu.4 (Tailscale WhoIs middleware)

These are merged into this branch for the complete feature.

author: elcallio
body:
Refs #27429
    
Re-implement the dtest with same name as a scylla pytest, using a python level network proxy instead of tcpdump etc. 
Both to avoid sudo and also to ensure we don't race.

Juggles different listen_address and broadcast_address values to insert a proxy measuring RPC traffic.

Note: the measuring relies on python network IO not splitting data chunks, since we don't really have packet-level view of the connections.

Note that a scylla change is required to make the ip address magic work, otherwise topology mechanism gets
confused. This should maybe at some point be looked into more, since we should be more resilient against various services in scylla binding to different addresses.

When this test is merged, we can drop the flaky test from dtest. And hope no new flakiness comes from this one...

## Are you drafting a new FIP?
Please follow these guidelines to help ensure that your proposal is set up for success in the governance process.

### Open a discussion topic
Changes to the Filecoin core protocol proceed through open discussion.
Please open a new discussion topic in the FIPs repository discussion board and outline you motivation and proposal.

The FIP format is suitable for specifying a concrete protocol change for implementation, 
but your discussion post should describe more of the background and problem to be solved,
outline a range of approaches and their tradeoffs, and invite participants to explore other solutions.

Historically, failing to gain some community buy-in before submitting a FIP has often resulted in 
rejected FIPs and much wasted effort.

### Please use the template
Please draft your FIP by starting with an appropriate template file from templates directory.
Do not significantly change the header table format or section headings.

### Don't claim a FIP number
FIP numbers are allocated by the FIP editors when a draft is ready to be merged into the master branch.
The editors coordinate to ensure allocations to in-flight drafts don't collide.
Please do not allocate yourself a FIP number.

Name your file `fip-my_draft_title.md` (replacing the suffix with an abbreviated title)
and leave "to be assigned" for the FIP number in the header table.
A FIP editor will either inform you of the appropriate number, or insert it themselves when merging.

### Please add your FIP to the README
The top-level README.md file contains a table of all FIPs.
Please add yours there in the same PR that adds the FIP draft itself.
Use XXXX for the FIP number until it is assigned by an editor.

### Delete this guidance and describe your FIP
Once you've followed the guidance above and are ready to submit your FIP draft,
please delete this text and replace it with a copy of the _Abstract_ from your draft, 
and a link to the relevant discussion forum topic.

author: pentop
body:
## Summary

Add `daemonClient.ResolveID()` calls before `AddComment` and `ListComments` operations in daemon mode, following the pattern from `update.go`, `label.go`, and other commands.

## Problem

Short IDs (e.g., `5wbm`) worked with most `bd` commands but failed with `comments add` and `comments list` when using the daemon:

```bash
# This works
bd update 5wbm --status in_progress

# This failed
bd comments add 5wbm "My comment"
# Error: adding comment: operation failed: failed to add comment: issue 5wbm not found
```

The short ID was passed directly to the RPC server which expected full IDs (e.g., `prefix-5wbm`).

## Solution

Add ID resolution before daemon RPC calls in both `commentsCmd` (list) and `commentsAddCmd` (add), matching the pattern used by other commands:

```go
if daemonClient != nil {
    // Resolve short/partial ID to full ID before sending to daemon (#1070)
    resolveArgs := &rpc.ResolveIDArgs{ID: issueID}
    resolveResp, err := daemonClient.ResolveID(resolveArgs)
    // ...
    issueID = resolvedID
    
    // Now call with resolved ID
    resp, err := daemonClient.AddComment(...)
}
```

## Changes

- `cmd/bd/comments.go`: Add ID resolution before daemon RPC calls for both `comments add` and `comments list`
- `internal/rpc/comments_test.go`: Update tests to reflect client-side resolution pattern (RPC server expects full IDs, CLI resolves first)

## Test Plan

- [x] `TestCLI_CommentsAddShortID` - CLI tests with short ID, partial ID, and comment alias
- [x] `TestCommentAddWithResolvedID` - RPC test simulating CLI workflow
- [x] `TestCommentListWithResolvedID` - RPC test for list operation
- [x] All existing comment tests still pass

Fixes #1070
