This PR optimizes the DSP diagram layout specifically for 1920x1080 landscape video presentations, ensuring the complete SVG diagram is visible while maximizing vertical space.

## Changes Made

Modified `osf/apps/osf-ui/src/app/components/dsp-animation/dsp-animation.component.html`, `dsp-animation.component.scss`, `dsp-animation.component.ts`, and `osf/apps/osf-ui/src/app/pages/dsp/customer/shared/customer-page.styles.ts`:

### 1. Minimized White Space
- **Diagram wrapper height**: Reduced `max-height` from `99vh` to `70vh`
- **Container padding**: Reduced from `1.5rem` to `1rem 1rem 0.5rem 1rem` (with minimal bottom padding)
- **Element spacing**: Reduced gap between flex elements from `1.5rem` to `0.5rem`
- **Diagram padding**: Reduced from `1rem` to `0.5rem`
- **SVG minimum height**: Reduced from `400px` to `300px`

### 2. Navigation Controls Moved to Header (Maximum Vertical Space)
Moved all navigation controls from footer to header to maximize vertical space for the diagram:
- **Header Layout**: 3-column grid with Title | Navigation Controls | Zoom Controls
- **Navigation Controls**: Compact circular icon buttons (◀ ▶ ↺ ▶) for Previous, Play/Pause, Loop, Next
- **Footer Removed**: Eliminated entire footer section to free up vertical space
- **Step Information**: Already displayed in SVG overlay (green banner at top of diagram)

### 3. Zoom Step Size Adjustment
- **5% increments** when zoom ≤ 100% (for finer control)
- **10% increments** when zoom > 100%
- Extracted to named constants (`ZOOM_STEP_FINE`, `ZOOM_STEP_COARSE`) with JSDoc documentation

### 4. Compact Header Design
- Reduced title font size: 1.5rem → 1.25rem
- Reduced subtitle font size: 0.875rem → 0.8rem
- Smaller zoom controls: 32px → 28px buttons
- Tighter spacing throughout all header elements
- Added navigation controls as 32px circular icon buttons

### 5. Customer DSP Pages Optimization
- **Page padding**: Reduced from `2rem` to `1rem`
- **Header margins**: Reduced from `2rem` to `1rem`
- **H1 font size**: Reduced from `2rem` to `1.5rem`
- **Button sizing**: Reduced padding and added consistent font sizing (`0.875rem`)
- **View mode selector**: Reduced top margin from `1rem` to `0.75rem`

## Scope

These changes affect all DSP diagram views across the application:
- Main DSP tab with 3 views (Architecture/Funktionsansicht, Components/Komponentenansicht, Deployment)
- FMF customer page (`dsp/customer/fmf`)
- ECME customer page (`dsp/customer/ecme`)

## Technical Details

- CSS Grid used for 3-column header layout with inline documentation
- Navigation controls styled as compact 32px circular buttons with icon symbols
- Dynamic zoom step calculation based on current zoom level
- Removed ~120 lines of footer control styles
- All changes are visual/layout only - no logic changes to diagram rendering or animation
- Customer pages automatically inherit component-level optimizations

## Benefits

- **Maximum vertical space**: Entire footer section eliminated
- **Compact design**: All controls consolidated in single header row
- **Better 1920x1080 fit**: Complete SVG diagram visible with no wasted space below
- **Clean interface**: Step information integrated into SVG overlay
- **Preserved functionality**: All navigation features remain accessible

## Testing

- ✅ All code review issues resolved
- ✅ No security vulnerabilities detected (CodeQL analysis passed)
- ✅ TypeScript compilation passes successfully
- ✅ Comprehensive JSDoc documentation added
- ✅ All navigation functionality preserved

The changes successfully optimize the layout for 1920x1080 landscape video presentations with maximum vertical space for the diagram while maintaining full functionality and responsiveness across all views and customer pages.

author: danersharifi-fr
body:
### Motivation
- Future-dated Allo windows should be considered active in the catalog so students can reserve slots before the window start as long as the window hasn't ended.
- Current logic required the current time to be between window start and end which hid future services and prevented reservations for upcoming windows.

### Description
- Updated `server/app/Http/Controllers/Api/AlloApiController.php` to compute `is_window_open` as `window_end_at` exists and `now <= window_end_at` and to only reject bookings when `now > window_end_at`.
- Updated client-side logic in `server/resources/views/allos.blade.php` to make `isWindowOpen` check only `window_end_at` and `now <= end` so future windows are shown as active.
- Resulting behavior: Allos whose window starts in the future remain visible and reservable until their `window_end_at`, while bookings are still blocked after the window end.

### Testing

author: deftruth
body:
follows up #12702, make qwen-image cp_plan compatible with txt_seq_lens, attn_mask and modulate_index(zero_cond_t)

- 1. Change the CP plan from transformer-level to block-level to avoid sequence length mismatch in rope and compute_text_seq_len_from_mask.
- 2. Relax the attn_mask limit in context_parallel. Since we have already done the checks in the attention backend, there is no need to do additional checks in context_parallel. This can bring more opportunities for performance optimization, especially for cases with attn_mask. 
- 3. In the case of qwen, attn_mask was processed before context_parallel and was not affected by sequence splitting. Therefore, we do not need to perform additional processing on its attn_mask.
- 4. This modification is universal for the qwen series, regardless of whether attn_mask is present or not.
- 5. Make CP plan compatible with zero_cond_t (introduced by Qwen-Image-Edit-2511)
- 6. Tested on Qwen-Image && Qwen-Image-2512 && Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 && Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 &&  Qwen-Image-Layered, confirm it is working as expected.

@sayakpaul @kashif 

## Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 && Qwen-Image-Edit-2511

```python
import torch
import argparse
from diffusers.utils import load_image
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
import torch.distributed as dist
from diffusers import ContextParallelConfig

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test Qwen-Image-Edit with Context Parallelism")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--use_2511",
        action="store_true",
        help="Use Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 model if set, otherwise use 2509 model.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()

args = parse_args()

if dist.is_available():
    dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl")
    rank = dist.get_rank()
    device = torch.device("cuda", rank % torch.cuda.device_count())
    world_size = dist.get_world_size()
    torch.cuda.set_device(device)
else:
    rank = 0
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    world_size = 1

if args.use_2511:
    model_id = "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511"
else:
    model_id = "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509"

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    model_id, 
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload(device=device)

pipe.transformer.set_attention_backend("native")
if world_size > 1:
    from diffusers import QwenImageTransformer2DModel
    assert isinstance(pipe.transformer, QwenImageTransformer2DModel)
    pipe.transformer.enable_parallelism(
        config=ContextParallelConfig(ulysses_degree=world_size)
    )

pipe.set_progress_bar_config(disable=rank != 0)

image1 = load_image("https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit/raw/main/examples/data/edit2509_1.jpg")
image2 = load_image("https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit/raw/main/examples/data/edit2509_2.jpg")
prompt = "The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square"
inputs = {
    "image": [image1, image2],
    "prompt": prompt,
    "generator": torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(0),
    "true_cfg_scale": 4.0,
    "negative_prompt": " ",
    "num_inference_steps": 50,
    "num_images_per_prompt": 1,
    "height": 1024,
    "width": 1024,
}

with torch.inference_mode():
    output = pipe(**inputs)
    output_image = output.images[0]
    model_version = "2511" if args.use_2511 else "2509"
    if world_size > 1:
        save_path = f"output_image_edit_{model_version}_ulysses{world_size}.png"
    else:
        save_path = f"output_image_edit_{model_version}.png"
    if rank == 0:
        output_image.save(save_path)
        print(f"image saved at {save_path}")

if dist.is_initialized():
    dist.destroy_process_group()
```

- test cmds:

```bash
torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 --local-ranks-filter=0 test_qwen_edit.py # baseline edit_2509
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 --local-ranks-filter=0 test_qwen_edit.py # cp4 edit_2509
torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 --local-ranks-filter=0 test_qwen_edit.py --use_2511 # baseline edit_2511
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 --local-ranks-filter=0 test_qwen_edit.py --use_2511 # cp4 edit_2511
```

L'uploader de piwigo change systématiquement l'extension jps du fichier que j'upload en jpg.

Je ne souhaite pas que piwigo prenne des initiatives de renommage que je doit gérer moi même. C'est pourquoi je propose l'introduction de ce trigger. Cela ne change en rien le fonctionnement de Piwigo si le callback n'est pas exécuté, mais permet de traiter des formats de fichiers non prévus...
Merci de votre compréhension

author: copilot
body:
Image blocks using the same CSV column were sharing cached images due to cache key mismatch between client and server. Additionally, missing placeholders left blank spaces when images failed to load, and transient network failures had no retry mechanism.

## Changes

### Cache Key Alignment
- Synchronized client `buildImageKey` and server `buildImageCacheKey` parameter order
- Added `elementId` to API request/response pipeline to differentiate image blocks

**Before:**
```javascript
// Client: [elementId, refValue, template, selector, ...]
// Server: [refValue, template, selector, ..., elementId]  
// → Keys don't match, cache collision
```

**After:**
```javascript
// Both: [refValue, template, selector, ..., csvColumn, elementId]
// → Consistent cache keys, blocks isolated
```

### Failure Handling
- Added retry logic (2 attempts, 1s delay) for transient network failures
- Implemented cache validation to reject null/invalid entries
- Added placeholders for all failure states (missing reference, failed load, loading)

### Code Quality
- Extracted `buildImagePlaceholder(baseStyle, message, bgColor)` helper to eliminate duplication
- Replaced React `innerHTML` manipulation with state-based rendering

## Example

Template with two image blocks using `REF` column:
```javascript
Block 1: selector=".main-image", elementId="elem-123"
Block 2: selector=".thumbnail", elementId="elem-456"

// Cache keys are now distinct:
"ABC123|...|.main-image|...|REF|elem-123"
"ABC123|...|.thumbnail|...|REF|elem-456"
```

Each block independently fetches and caches its image.

### Motivation

- The video resizer download buttons were inconsistent and could fail in some browsers because they used the wrong URL for proxy downloads. 
- Thumbnails for generated video versions sometimes did not appear, leaving blank list items. 
- The video preview/modal and tool panels needed a more modern, polished look and subtle animations for better UX. 

### Description

- Use the version source URL (fallback to `downloadUrl`) when building the proxy download URL and guard against missing URLs in `VideoResizer` (`client/src/components/CreativeStudio.jsx`).
- Add `thumbnailErrors` state and render a short preview `video` element as a fallback when `version.thumbnail` is missing or fails to load, and mark failing images via `onError` to avoid repeated broken requests. 
- Add safer link attributes (`rel="noopener"` and `target="_blank"`) when programmatically clicking download anchors to improve cross-browser consistency. 
- Polish styles: gradient header, hover/transition effects on cards and buttons, and a blurred backdrop + elevated modal (`backdrop-blur-sm`, shadows and borders) for a modern appearance.

### Motivation
- Replace the single flat ground fill with per-lane rendering so segmented terrain produced by the runtime is visually clear and supports gameplay intent. 
- Visually distinguish safe vs unsafe spans so players can more easily read beat-aligned safe pads and avoid gaps. 
- Preserve existing lead-in overlays tied to the intensity window and add subtle parallax so vertical tiers remain legible. 
- Provide documentation and tests to cover the new rendering behavior.

### Description
- Reworked `drawWorld` to consume `runtime.groundSegments` (grouped by `levelIndex`) and draw each lane segment instead of a single `runtime.groundY` fill. 
- Added visual treatments: unsafe spans use a lower alpha and dashed interior strokes, while safe spans get a beat-synced pulse highlight driven by `ui.beatPulse`. 
- Introduced small per-lane x-offset parallax to separate vertical tiers, and kept lead-in overlays tied to the intensity window (`runtime.intensityLeadInActive` or `intensityWindow`). 
- Added `docs/rendering.md`, a README note, a unit test `src/game/render/drawWorld.test.ts`, updated `src/game/loop.test.ts` fixtures, and a small formatting tweak to `drawShockwaves` in `drawEffects.ts`.

body:
## Synopsis

This adds the possibility to use custom functions to perform the equality check in `PartialEq`/`Eq` derives. This is quite useful when wrapping types without a `PartialEq`/`Eq` impl

## Solution

This builds on #532 and reuse the `FieldAttributes` for `Hash`, I moved the struct to `utils::attr` and renamed it `WithOrSkip`.

I removed fields types that have a `with` attribute from the automatically added `where Type: Eq` bound automatically generated by the `Eq` derive. This seems like the thing to do as if you're using a custom function it most probably means the field doesn't implement `Eq`.  

While this is not part of the roadmap for PartialEq, defined in #163 this is something that will be quite useful for people migrating form `derivative` as this was something supported by this crate

body:
Implements conversational calendar management using AI SDK tool calling with interactive generative UI components for event creation, editing, and confirmation.

## Calendar Tools (`ai/calendar-tools.ts`)
- 9 Google Calendar API tools: draft, create, list, update, delete, find availability, get event
- OAuth 2.0 flow via `/api/auth/google/*` routes
- CRUD operations through `/api/calendar/*` endpoints

## Generative UI Components
- **EventSchedulingConfirmation** - Human-in-the-loop approval form with editable fields and AI reasoning display
- **CalendarEvent** - Animated success card for created events
- Auto-rendering in `message-list.tsx` based on tool invocation type

## Chat Integration
- Tool activation via `@calendar` mentions
- Streamlined system prompts (removed verbose scheduling instructions)
- Tools registered dynamically in `/api/chat/route.ts`

```tsx
// User: "schedule a meeting tomorrow at 2pm"
// AI calls scheduleCalendarEvent tool
<EventSchedulingConfirmation
  toolCallId={id}
  eventDetails={{
    title: "Meeting",
    startDateTime: "2026-01-14T14:00:00",
    endDateTime: "2026-01-14T15:00:00"
  }}
  reasoning="Inferred 1-hour duration from context"
/>
// User reviews, edits if needed, confirms → createCalendarEvent → CalendarEvent component
```

## Tech Stack
- AI SDK v5 `tool()` with Zod schemas
- Framer Motion animations
- Google Calendar API v3
- date-fns for formatting

<!-- Thanks so much for your PR, your contribution is appreciated! ❤️ -->


### Description:

 Root Cause

  When exporting a dashboard with only a specific tab selected (via selectedTabs URL parameter):

  1. MinimalDashboard filtered tiles using schedulerTabsSelected (e.g., second tab's UUID)
  2. DashboardProvider calculated expectedScreenshotTileUuids using activeTab which defaulted to first tab
  3. The screenshot ready indicator waited for first tab's tiles to report ready, but only second tab's tiles were rendered
  4. Result: Screenshot never became "ready" → timeout → failure

  Fix

  1. Added schedulerTabsSelected prop to DashboardProvider
  2. Updated expectedScreenshotTileUuids to use schedulerTabsSelected when provided, so it waits for the correct tiles
  3. Passed schedulerTabsSelected from MinimalDashboard to DashboardProvider

- Stabilize layout by anchoring attacker nodes to the left column and removing alliance tags that clutter attacker labels.

body:
During bar length finding and evolutionary optimization, the browser appears frozen with no feedback, leaving users uncertain if the application is working.

## Changes

**Core library** (`src/utils/barLengthFinder.js`)
- Added `onProgress` callback parameter to `findOptimalLength()` 
- Callback fires each iteration with: `{iteration, maxIterations, currentLength, currentFrequency, errorCents, searchRange}`
- Documented with JSDoc typedef `LengthSearchProgress`

**Interactive demo** (`demo.html`)
- CSS: progress bars, spinners, status text
- HTML: progress containers for Bar Length Finder and Optimization Path tabs
- JS: integrated callbacks to update UI, disable buttons during computation

**Console demo** (`example_usage.js`)
- Added progress logging to Example 9 (every 5th iteration)

## Usage

```javascript
findOptimalLength(
    220.0,  // target frequency
    38,     // width
    25,     // thickness
    material,
    200, 800, 1.0, 50, 80,
    undefined, 0.0, 2, 3,
    (progress) => {
        console.log(`Iteration ${progress.iteration}: ${progress.currentFrequency.toFixed(2)}Hz`);
        progressBar.style.width = `${progress.iteration / progress.maxIterations * 100}%`;
    }
);
```

## Screenshots

**Before**: No indication of progress during computation
![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/259665c5-2887-4c52-aae1-c14b118afebc)

**After**: Visual feedback with progress bar and live updates
![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87aa1ef2-cff7-4d33-92c4-37b6a20bfc55)

## Note

JavaScript's single-threaded execution limits UI responsiveness during synchronous computation. Progress callbacks execute but DOM updates may batch until completion. For production with heavier workloads, consider Web Workers or computation chunking via `requestAnimationFrame`.

author: lourq
body:
## Summary
- Modified `getErrorRSCPayload()` to properly server-render the not-found page content when `notFound()` is called in a Server Component
- For 404 errors, now uses `createNotFoundLoaderTree()` and `createComponentTree()` to generate actual page content (same approach as Server Action notFound handling)
- Other error types (redirect, 403, 401, 500) preserve the original empty skeleton behavior

## Problem
When `notFound()` was called in a Server Component, the 404 page was being rendered on the client (CSR) instead of the server (SSR). The HTML response contained only scripts and empty body, requiring client-side hydration.

### Root Cause
`getErrorRSCPayload()` created a hardcoded empty HTML skeleton:
```typescript
const seedData: CacheNodeSeedData = [
  createElement('html', { id: '__next_error__' },
    createElement('head', null),
    createElement('body', null, null) // EMPTY!
  ),
  {}, null, false, false
]
```

While the Server Action path correctly used `createNotFoundLoaderTree()` + `renderToStream()` to render full content.

## Solution
For 404 errors specifically, `getErrorRSCPayload()` now:
1. Creates `notFoundLoaderTree` using `createNotFoundLoaderTree()`
2. Calls `createComponentTree()` with the not-found loader tree to generate actual seedData
3. Returns proper RSC payload with rendered not-found page content

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify that `notFound()` in Server Component returns full HTML (SSR)
- [ ] Check that 404 status code is correctly set
- [ ] Test in both dev and production modes
- [ ] Ensure other error types (403, 401, redirect, 500) still work correctly

Fixes #62228

author: pgellert
body:
This PR continues making the Schema Registry context-aware by migrating all `/subjects/...` handlers and the compatibility endpoint to parse subjects as context-qualified subjects, enabling the `:.context:subject` syntax.

This is the first PR where user-visible changes are introduced: users can now register and query schemas using qualified subjects (e.g., `:.staging:my-topic-value`), with each context maintaining its own independent schema ID counter.

### The key changes are:
  - All subject path parameters in handlers are now parsed using `context_subject::from_string()`, enabling qualified subject syntax
  - Schema references in request bodies are also parsed as context-qualified, enabling cross-context references
  - Schema ID lookups and existence checks are now context-scoped (`get_schema_id(ctx, ...)`, `has_schema(context_schema_id{ctx, id})`)
  - Swagger documentation updated to describe the qualified subject format for all subject parameters

### Not yet implemented:
 - Parent-context-based context-determination for references with unqualified subjects

author: makobcki
body:
### Motivation
- Speed up and make `scripts/prepare_latents.py` more robust and observable by moving disk writes off the GPU path and emitting fine-grained performance metrics. 
- Enable workflows that do not require captions/tags by adding an `images_only` indexing mode so images can be prepared/trained without metadata. 
- Support large latent caches via a sharded on-disk format and index to reduce overhead when training from precomputed latents. 
- Make text conditioning and self-conditioning runtime-configurable and add a cosine noise schedule option for sampling.

### Description
- Add `images_only` to `TrainConfig` and implement an images-only index path in `diffusion/data.py` that emits entries with empty `caption`/tag fields and caches the index; propagate `images_only` into `scripts/train.py` and `scripts/prepare_latents.py` via `DanbooruConfig` and `TrainConfig` (see `config/train.yaml`, `diffusion/config.py`, `diffusion/data.py`, `scripts/train.py`, `scripts/prepare_latents.py`).
- Rewrite `scripts/prepare_latents.py` to use an asynchronous save queue and optional `_ShardWriter` with `--shard-size` to produce sharded latent `.pt` files and a JSONL shard index, add `--decode-backend`, use `torch.inference_mode()`+autocast, batch CPU copies, and emit detailed metrics (decode/h2d/encode/save timings).
- Add sharded latent cache support to `DanbooruDataset` with a shard index loader and `latent_cache_sharded`/`latent_cache_index_path` wiring so training can read sharded latent files efficiently, and make latent loading robust to missing entries and fallback encoding.
- Make text-conditioning optional across sampling/train code paths by threading `use_text_conditioning` through checkpoints/metadata and adjusting `UNet`, samplers and collate logic to accept `txt_ids`/`txt_mask` as optional, add `NoOpCrossAttention` and self-conditioning hooks, add `noise_schedule`/`cosine_s` to `DiffusionConfig`, and add related config options and runtime behavior (see `diffusion/model.py`, `diffusion/ddim.py`, `diffusion/diffusion.py`, `diffusion/domain.py`, `scripts/sample.py`, `scripts/train.py`).
- Misc: replace fragile `eval`/`repr` index writes with JSON, add safer latent validation, expose checkpoint info endpoint in web UI and disable/grey-out prompt inputs when a checkpoint indicates text-conditioning is disabled (see `webui/backend/app.py`, `webui/frontend/*`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change set.
- Manual expectations (not executed here): `scripts/prepare_latents.py --shard-size` should produce sharded `.pt` files and an `index.jsonl`, and `scripts/prepare_latents.py` with `--decode-backend` should respect the chosen decoder; `scripts/train.py` should run with `images_only=true` and `use_text_conditioning=false` using the image-only index.

author: skandas1304
body: ### Summary This PR introduces a Bayesian state-space tyre degradation model for the race replay system. - The model introduces a latent-state formulation as an alternative to heuristic or curve-smoothed approaches The implementation is inspired by recent state-space approaches used in motorsport analytics and is designed to be robust to noisy race telemetry. --- ### Model overview Tyre performance is modeled as a latent pace state that evolves lap-by-lap: - Degradation is treated as a stochastic process rather than a fixed curve - Lap times are observations of the latent state, corrupted by noise - A Kalman filter is used to update the latent pace in real time - Compound-specific degradation rates are learned from data This allows degradation behavior to adapt naturally across tracks, compounds, and stint lengths. > **Note: This model applies to slick tyres only (Soft, Medium, Hard). > Wet and Intermediate tyres are excluded because lap times in wet conditions depend primarily on track wetness evolution, tyre mismatch effects, and non-monotonic performance changes, which are not captured by a degradation-driven state-space model.** --- ### Health vs degradation (important clarification) The UI exposes a **“tyre health”** value derived from the model output. This value does **not** represent physical tyre wear or “tyre life remaining”. Instead, it represents **distance from peak performance** within a strategy-relevant window. Key implications: - A tyre reaching 0% health does not mean it is unusable - It means the tyre is no longer near its optimal performance window - Teams may (and often do) continue running tyres well past this point for strategic reasons This distinction is especially important for tracks like Mexico, where thermal effects cause early loss of peak pace but tyres remain usable for many laps. --- ### Track-dependent behavior The model intentionally produces different degradation signatures depending on circuit characteristics: - Bahrain: high effective degradation due to abrasion and traction - COTA: moderate degradation with strong compound separation - Mexico: low mechanical wear but rapid thermal performance drop on soft tyres These effects emerge naturally from the data rather than being hard-coded. --- ### Paper reference The structure of this model is inspired by state-space approaches to tyre degradation modeling, in particular: > Cole Cappello, Andrew Hoegh (2025) > *A State-Space Approach to Modeling Tire Degradation in Formula 1 Racing* > https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00640 While this implementation uses a fast MAP-style estimation suitable for real-time replay, the architecture allows future extension to full Bayesian inference (e.g. PyMC / Stan). --- ### Integration details - The Bayesian model is fully encapsulated in `bayesian_tyre_model.py` - A thin integrator layer preserves the existing UI and rendering logic - No major UI changes are required to adopt the new model - Degradation uncertainty is explicitly estimated and can be surfaced if needed --- ### Validation The model was tested on multiple races with expected qualitative behavior: - Correct compound ordering (HARD < MEDIUM < SOFT) - Higher degradation at abrasive circuits - Thermal-dominated degradation at high-altitude tracks This confirms the model behaves realistically across track types. --- After the addition of the tyre health bar A demo video at 128x ( taken at 128x to achieve a video size less than 10MB) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb13c998-27ae-40b1-814f-b17589c97afd

## Summary
Implements a production-ready tile caching system with S3+Redis hybrid backend, admin API, and comprehensive Helm chart support. Provides performance improvements for tile requests.

## Features Added
- **Multi-Backend Caching**: Redis-only, S3-only, and S3+Redis hybrid configurations
- **Admin API**: RESTful cache management with pattern-based invalidation at `/admin/cache/*`
- **Production Helm Chart**: Complete cache configuration with validation and examples
- **TTL Management**: Configurable expiration for tiles (3600s) and datasets (1800s)
- **Graceful Fallback**: Cache failures don't break tile serving (X-Cache headers for monitoring)

## Implementation Details
- **Cache System**: `titiler/cache/` module with pluggable backends
- **Key Generation**: Tiling-aware with parameter exclusion and namespace support  
- **Middleware**: Transparent tile caching with 2048-char key support
- **S3 Backend**: Isolated credentials, dedicated bucket `esa-sentinel-zarr-explorer-cache`
- **Redis Backend**: Metadata storage with TTL countdown and pattern matching

## Configuration
### Development (Redis-only)
```bash
helm install titiler-eopf ./helm -f examples/cache-redis-values.yaml
```

### Production (S3+Redis)
```bash
helm install titiler-eopf ./helm -f examples/cache-s3-redis-values.yaml
```

None. Backward compatible with existing deployments.

Ready for staging deployment. Cache system fully validated in local environment with Docker Redis and S3 backend.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

Implements Tensor Logic framework concepts from https://tensor-logic.org/ and Ben Goertzel's neural-symbolic integration work as a native PowerShell module.

## Core Module (`src/TensorLogic/Module/TensorLogic.psm1`)

- **Tensor Operations**: Multi-dimensional tensor creation, initialization, and Einstein summation (matrix multiplication)
- **Logical Operations**: Fuzzy logic over tensors (AND=min, OR=max, NOT=complement, IMPLIES)
- **Knowledge Bases**: Facts and relations encoded as tensor structures
- **Reasoning Engine**: Multi-step inference via matrix-vector multiplication with confidence propagation

## API

```powershell
# Classical logic reasoning
$kb = New-SymbolicKnowledgeBase -Facts @("Socrates", "Man", "Mortal")
Add-SymbolicRelation -KnowledgeBase $kb -RelationName "isA" -FromFact "Socrates" -ToFact "Man"
Add-SymbolicRelation -KnowledgeBase $kb -RelationName "isA" -FromFact "Man" -ToFact "Mortal"
$result = Invoke-SymbolicReasoning -KnowledgeBase $kb -Query "Socrates" -RelationChain @("isA", "isA")
# → Infers: Socrates is Mortal with confidence 1.0

# Probabilistic reasoning with fuzzy logic
$evidence1 = New-Tensor -Dimensions @(3) -Values @(0.9, 0.7, 0.5)
$evidence2 = New-Tensor -Dimensions @(3) -Values @(0.8, 0.6, 0.4)
$combined = Invoke-TensorLogicRule -Rule "AND" -InputTensors @($evidence1, $evidence2)
# → Result: [0.8, 0.6, 0.4] (conservative confidence via min)
```

## Testing & Documentation

- 18 standalone unit tests (all passing)
- Module manifest with PowerShell 5.1+ compatibility
- Comprehensive README with examples and theoretical background
- Working demonstration script showing classical logic, probabilistic inference, and fuzzy operations

## Implementation Notes

- Pure PowerShell implementation using hashtables for tensor representation
- No external dependencies (ML.NET, ONNX, or Python)
- Knowledge graphs represented as adjacency matrices
- Relation chaining via repeated matrix multiplication
- Fixed array arithmetic in reasoning functions (explicit scalar extraction)

This pull request updates and streamlines the project's development environment, focusing on modernizing the CMake configuration, build, and debugging workflows. The changes standardize on CMake presets, switch to the `lldb` debugger, and simplify related VSCode tasks and settings for a more maintainable and consistent experience across platforms.

**Development environment modernization:**

- Migrated all build and configuration logic to use CMake presets, introducing a new `CMakePresets.json` with a `base` preset (using Ninja and Clang) and a simplified `debug` preset. Removed older, redundant, or CI-specific presets for clarity and maintainability.
- Refactored `.vscode/tasks.json` to use the new CMake presets for configuration and building, consolidating multiple build tasks into a few generic ones and removing separate Debug/Release/CI tasks.

**Debugging improvements:**

- Updated `.vscode/launch.json` to use the `lldb` debugger instead of `cppdbg`/GDB, simplified launch configurations, and improved Windows compatibility. Removed rarely used or redundant debug configurations.
- Added the `vadimcn.vscode-lldb` extension to `.vscode/extensions.json` to support the new debugger workflow.

**VSCode settings and IntelliSense:**

- Added a `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` file to specify C/C++ standards (`c23`, `c++26`) and integration with CMake Tools, ensuring consistent IntelliSense and code navigation.
- Updated `.vscode/settings.json` to always use CMake presets, enable advanced options, and remove explicit compiler path settings for improved portability.

**Minor code fix:**

- Fixed a potential crash in `SoundManager::loadAll()` by ensuring `_music` is initialized before use.

author: conniecombs
body:
fix: Replace math/rand with crypto/rand for jitter calculation

This commit addresses the golangci-lint security warning about using
weak random number generator (math/rand) by replacing it with crypto/rand.

**Changes:**
- Replace mathrand.Float64() with crypto/rand in calculateBackoff()
- Remove math/rand import (no longer needed)
- Use crypto/rand to generate 8 random bytes
- Convert random bytes to float64 in range [0, 1)
- Apply jitter calculation as before: ±20% range

**Technical Details:**
- Read 8 bytes from crypto/rand
- Convert to uint64 by combining bytes
- Scale to [0, 1) range: float64(randUint) / float64(^uint64(0))
- Apply jitter: (randFloat * 0.4) - 0.2 for ±20%
- Fallback to no jitter if crypto/rand fails (unlikely)

**Security:**
- Eliminates weak random number generator warning
- Uses cryptographically secure random source
- Maintains same jitter behavior for backoff algorithm

While math/rand is technically acceptable for non-security-sensitive
jitter, using crypto/rand ensures compliance with security linters
and follows defense-in-depth principles.

body:
## 🗒️ Summary
Initial implementation of password expiration checking support, provided by an AWS EventBridge Schedule invoking an AWS Lambda function. This function examines user history (which must be enabled in the respective user pool) to determine if there is an event constituting a password change in the configured amount of days. If not, the user's state is changed to force password change and an associated email message is sent to the user. Additionally, if a password change event has not occurred within n days before expiration, a warning email message is generated and sent.

The benefit of enforcing password change is under significant debate - arguments against are that routine password rotation encourages users to utilize weak and/or predictable patterns. While elimination of this enforcement is not yet official, it seems likely that this will occur soon, possibly in the current FY26. PDS' intention is to deploy and test the mechanism (in a manner that does not affect changes but instead only logs findings and intentions), then deactivate the EventBridge Schedule. The notion behind this is that should a compromise of passwords be suspected, the Schedule can be re-enabled such that all users will be forced to reset their passwords.

One enhancement that is acknowledged but not implemented is the division of users across multiple child-Lambda executions. There is a point at which the number of users will cause the single Lambda to exceed the maximum execution time of 15 minutes - through division of effort, the violation of this time maximum can be avoided.

Some reorganization and changes to other cognito-related scripts have been made, namely those now residing in the userpool_mgt subdirectory. These are not related to or utilized by the password expiration checking.

## ⚙️ Test Data and/or Report
In a reversal of convention and practice, after deployment and close observation of this mechanism in dev/test environments, this has been deployed in production - again, with the log-only strategy described above. The logs have been scoured with results being as expected. The Schedule has now been deactivated.

Resolves nasa-PDS/planetary-data-cloud#117

body:
## Summary

This PR contains critical fixes and improvements to the MCP stdio bridge to make it work properly with Claude Code.

### Root Cause & Fix

The main issue was that tool call responses were not following the MCP specification format. Per [MCP spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools), tool responses must have:
```json
{
  "result": {
    "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

The ProxySQL MCP server was returning raw data instead, causing Claude Code to timeout waiting for properly formatted responses.

### Changes

**C++ Server (lib/MCP_Endpoint.cpp):**

body:
## 🎯 Summary

Implements complete support for **Shenzhen Jinling Electronics Co., Ltd. (JILN)** connectors with handlers for both elprint position-based encoding (15 chars) and distributor format MPNs (15-18 chars) used on LCSC/JLCPCB platforms.

**Test Results**: ✅ 131/131 tests passing (100%) | ✅ 13,122 total tests passing | ✅ 0 regressions

---

## 📦 What's New

### JinlingHandler.java (~560 lines)
- ✅ **Dual Format Support**: Elprint (27310202ANG3SUT) + Distributor (22850102ANG1SYA02) formats
- ✅ **Position-Based Extraction**: Decodes 15-character elprint with fixed position meanings
- ✅ **Exact Length Validation**: `length() != 15` check prevents both short AND long MPNs
- ✅ **15+ Helper Methods**: Pin count, pitch, gender, mounting type, orientation, materials, plating, post, packing, category
- ✅ **Replacement Logic**: Same family + pin count + compatible mounting types

### JinlingHandlerTest.java (~550 lines, 131 tests)
- ✅ **100% Pass Rate**: All tests passing after systematic MPN format corrections
- ✅ **13 Nested Test Classes**: Organized by category (families, extraction, helpers, replacement, edge cases)
- ✅ **Real-World MPNs**: Uses actual LCSC/JLCPCB distributor part numbers
- ✅ **Comprehensive Coverage**: Pattern matching, extraction, validation, replacement logic

### SKILL.md Documentation (~400 lines)
- ✅ **Company Overview**: Jinling background, specialization, 280+ patents
- ✅ **MPN Structure Diagrams**: ASCII diagrams showing all 15 positions
- ✅ **Complete Reference Tables**: Materials, plating grades, connector types, packing types
- ✅ **Real Examples**: LCSC MPNs with C-numbers (C601966, C429959, etc.)
- ✅ **Implementation Gotchas**: Position alignment, missing characters, validation strategies

---

## 🔍 Technical Deep Dive

### Position-Based Encoding Format

Jinling's elprint format uses a strict 15-character structure where **every position has meaning**:

```
27 31 0 2 02 A N G3 S U T
│  │  │ │ │  │ │ │  │ │ └─ [14] Packing (T/P/R/O/A)
│  │  │ │ │  │ │ │  │ └─── [13] ContactType (U/S/R)
│  │  │ │ │  │ │ │  └───── [12] ConnectorType (M/S/R/W/Z)
│  │  │ │ │  │ │ └─────── [10-11] ContactPlating (SN/G0-G5/S0)
│  │  │ │ │  │ └────────── [9] Post (W=with, N=without)
│  │  │ │ │  └─────────── [8] InsulatorMaterial (A-F)
│  │  │ │ └──────────── [6-7] PinsPerRow (00-99)
│  │  │ └────────────── [5] Rows (1-3)
│  │  └──────────────── [4] HouseCount (0)
│  └─────────────────── [2-3] PlasticsHeight × 10
└────────────────────── [0-1] Family (13/16/17/26/27)
```

**Example Decoding**: `27310202ANG3SUT`
- Family: 27 = 2.54mm female header
- Height: 31 = 3.1mm
- Rows: 2, Pins/Row: 02 → **4 total pins**
- Material: A = PBT
- Post: N = No post
- Plating: G3 = 10µin Gold
- Connector: S = Straight THT
- Contact: U = U-Type
- Packing: T = Tube

### Test Suite Journey

| Stage | Tests Passing | Failures | Root Cause |
|-------|--------------|----------|------------|
| Initial | 91/131 (69%) | 40 | MPN format violations |
| After pattern fix | 106/131 (81%) | 25 | Test MPNs still malformed |
| After MPN corrections | 122/131 (93%) | 9 | Orientation, distributor patterns |
| After distributor fix | 127/131 (97%) | 4 | Pin count, replacement logic |
| **Final** | **131/131 (100%)** | **0** | **All issues resolved** ✅ |

### Critical Gotchas Discovered

1. **Exact Length Matters**: Pattern must validate exactly 15 chars, not 13-17 variable range
2. **Numeric Positions**: Positions 2-7 (6 characters) MUST be numeric digits - letters break pin count extraction
3. **Position Alignment**: Moving a character one position breaks everything
   - Example: `27310202MNSNSUT` has "M" at position 8 (material) instead of position 12 (connector type)
4. **Missing Characters**: 14-char MPNs usually missing post indicator 'N' at position 9
   - Example: `17310110AG3SUT` → `17310110ANG3SUT`

### Pattern Evolution

```java
// ❌ WRONG (14 chars total, accepts variable length)
"^(?:13|16|17|26|27)[0-9]{4}[0-9]{2}[A-Z][A-Z]{2}[A-Z]{3}"

// ✅ CORRECT (15 chars: 2+6+1+1+2+3, exact length)
"^(?:13|16|17|26|27)[0-9]{6}[A-Z][A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}[A-Z]{3}$"
```

### Validation Strategy

```java
private boolean isElprintFormat(String mpn) {
    // CRITICAL: Check EXACT length, not just minimum
    if (mpn == null || mpn.length() != 15) return false;
    
    // Positions 2-7 must be ALL numeric (not just 2-5)
    boolean hasNumericPrefix = mpn.substring(2, 8).matches("[0-9]{6}");
    
    return isKnownFamily && hasNumericPrefix;
}
```

---

## 📊 Test Results

### Unit Tests
```
✅ JinlingHandlerTest: 131/131 passing (100%)
   ├─ Family 13 Tests: 7/7
   ├─ Family 16 Tests: 5/5
   ├─ Family 17 Tests: 8/8
   ├─ Family 26 Tests: 6/6
   ├─ Family 27 Tests: 9/9
   ├─ Distributor Format: 12/12
   ├─ Series Extraction: 8/8
   ├─ Package Code: 6/6
   ├─ Pin Count: 8/8
   ├─ Helper Methods: 47/47
   ├─ Replacement Logic: 6/6
   ├─ Edge Cases: 6/6
   └─ Initialization: 3/3
```

### Integration Tests
```
✅ Full test suite: 13,122 tests passing
✅ 0 failures
✅ 0 errors
✅ 3 skipped (expected)
✅ No regressions in existing handlers
```

---

## 📂 Files Changed

### New Files
- `src/main/java/.../manufacturers/JinlingHandler.java` (+560 lines)
- `src/test/java/.../handlers/JinlingHandlerTest.java` (+550 lines)
- `.claude/skills/manufacturers/jinling/SKILL.md` (+400 lines)

### Modified Files
- `src/main/java/.../ComponentManufacturer.java` (+1 line) - Added JINLING enum
- `src/main/java/.../ComponentType.java` (+2 lines) - Added CONNECTOR_JINLING type
- `README.md` (+1 word) - Added Jinling to Connectors section
- `CLAUDE.md` (+120 lines) - Added comprehensive learnings section

**Total**: +1,709 insertions, -1 deletion

---

## 🎓 Key Learnings

### Position-Based MPN Best Practices
1. **Pattern Design**: For position-based MPNs, validate EXACT length upfront, not ranges
2. **Test Data**: Use REAL distributor MPNs from LCSC/JLCPCB, not invented examples
3. **Incremental Testing**: Fix patterns first, then test MPNs, then extraction logic
4. **Documentation**: ASCII diagrams showing position meanings are invaluable
5. **Dual Format Support**: When manufacturer uses multiple formats, document both clearly

### Handler Implementation Insights
- Always check MPN length before substring operations (prevents IndexOutOfBoundsException)
- Use `length() != 15` not `length() < 15` to catch both short AND long MPNs
- Test failures with "expected: X but was: 0" often indicate missing characters at specific positions
- Position misalignment by 1 character can break everything - test MPNs must be exact

### Documentation Importance
- Position-by-position breakdown catches encoding errors early
- Real-world distributor examples provide validation baseline
- "Known Issues" section helps future developers avoid same pitfalls

---

## 🔄 Migration Guide

No migration needed - this is a purely additive feature.

### Usage Example

```java
// Detect Jinling connector
String mpn = "27310202ANG3SUT";
ComponentManufacturer mfr = ComponentManufacturer.fromMPN(mpn);
// Returns: ComponentManufacturer.JINLING

// Get handler

String gender = jinling.getGender(mpn);             // "Female"

String plating = jinling.getContactPlating(mpn);    // "10µin Gold"
String material = jinling.getInsulatorMaterial(mpn); // "PBT"
```

author: copilot
body:
Built a scalable CRM system with relational entities (Firms, Contacts, Projects), polymorphic notes, user tracking, global search, and filterable activity feed.

### Architecture

**Database models** (`models.py`):
- Users with note attribution
- Firms with industry and contact info
- Contacts belonging to firms (1:many)
- Projects linking firms and contacts (many:many via association table)
- Notes with polymorphic entity references (nullable FKs for firm/contact/project)

**Core features** (`app.py`):
- Global search using SQLAlchemy `ilike()` across all entities
- Activity feed with entity-type filtering (all/firms/contacts/projects)
- Full CRUD for firms, contacts, projects
- Notes system with timestamps and user attribution

**Data integrity**:
- Date parsing with error handling and flash messages
- Type validation for entity IDs with try/except blocks
- Contact-firm relationship enforcement on project associations
- Cascading deletes on relationships

### Example Usage

```python
# Polymorphic notes via nullable foreign keys
class Note(db.Model):
    firm_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('firms.id'), nullable=True)
    contact_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('contacts.id'), nullable=True)
    project_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('projects.id'), nullable=True)
    
    @property
    def entity_type(self):
        if self.firm_id: return 'Firm'
        elif self.contact_id: return 'Contact'
        elif self.project_id: return 'Project'
```

### Sample data
`init_db.py` seeds 3 firms, 4 contacts, 3 projects, 5 notes for immediate testing.

### Motivation
- Centralizar el almacenamiento de fotos en una entidad relacional para facilitar consultas y evitar JSON embebido en `reportes`.
- Reemplazar textos estáticos del layout por `env('APP_NAME')` y mostrar el logo para mejorar la consistencia de la marca en la interfaz.
- Simplificar el tablero retirando las secciones de “Municipios con más reportes” y “Tendencia semanal” para una vista ejecutiva más enfocada.
- Añadir relaciones Eloquent entre modelos para mejorar la navegabilidad de datos y la mantenibilidad del código.

### Description
- Añadido modelo `ReporteFoto` y migración `create_reportes_fotos` para almacenar rutas de imágenes en `reportes_fotos` y migración para eliminar la columna `fotos` de `reportes`.
- Migraciones y modelos: removido el campo JSON `fotos` de `Reporte`, creado `ReporteFoto` con `ruta`, y añadidas relaciones `fotos()`/`reportes()` en `Reporte`, `CatTipoReporte`, `cat_estado`, `cat_municipio` y `cat_colonia`.
- Actualizado `HomeController@store` para subir imágenes a `storage` y persistir registros en `reportes_fotos`, y adaptadas las consultas del `dashboard` para usar `whereHas('fotos')` y `with('fotos')` al obtener evidencia.

### Testing
- No se ejecutaron pruebas automatizadas debido a dependencias faltantes en el entorno; intento de levantar el servidor con `php artisan serve` falló por ausencia de `vendor/autoload.php`.
- Las migraciones nuevas están añadidas en `database/migrations` pero no fueron aplicadas (`php artisan migrate` no fue corrido en este entorno).

## **Summary**
- Sets up a consistent way to validate and review Terraform changes in this repository.
- Adds a simple quality gate, cleans up examples, and introduces a PR template to make reviews easier.

## **Context / Motivation**
- This repository is intended for open-source contributions, so we need a clear and predictable workflow.
- The goal is to catch common Terraform issues early and reduce back-and-forth during reviews.
- Local checks and CI now behave the same, so contributors know exactly what will run.

## **Type of Change**
- [x] CI / Tooling
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Example update

- [x] terraform fmt

- [x] tflint
- [ ] terratest (not applicable for this change)

## **Notes for Reviewers**
- Added a local `quality-gate.sh` script that runs formatting, validation, and linting.
- CI now runs the **same script** on PRs to `dev` and `main`.
- Cleaned up examples and module inputs to align with validation and lint rules.
- Removed deprecated examples to reduce maintenance noise.
- Added a PR template so future contributions follow a consistent structure.

- [x] Code follows module conventions
- [x] Inputs and outputs are documented
- [x] No secrets or sensitive data included

### Motivation
- Avoid committing binary artifacts by removing `faas/order-recommendation/function.zip` so PR diffs remain reviewable.
- Ensure the LocalStack init script builds the Lambda deployment package inside the container at startup to match the runtime environment.
- Keep the Lambda source (`faas/order-recommendation/handler.py`) versioned and reproducible by packaging it at init time.
- Prevent binary merge conflicts and reduce repository bloat.

- Deleted the committed binary `faas/order-recommendation/function.zip` from the repository.

- Left the Lambda source file `faas/order-recommendation/handler.py` in the repo so the init script can package it inside the LocalStack container.

body:
## Summary
- Add `run_lejepa_sweep.py` for running LeJEPA experiments across multiple model sizes and training checkpoints
- YAML-based configuration for flexible experiment sweeps
- Support for `epoch=N-step=M.ckpt` checkpoint format (PyTorch Lightning)
- Task-specific epoch sweeps (full checkpoint sweep on subset of tasks to save time)
- Parallel GPU execution with dry-run and resume modes

## Changes
- **New**: `run_lejepa_sweep.py` - Main sweep script
- **New**: `sweep_configs/` directory with 4 example configs:
  - `performance_over_training.yaml` - Track performance across training epochs
  - `full_benchmark.yaml` - Compare model sizes across all tasks
  - `combined_sweep.yaml` - Both epoch sweep + full benchmark
  - `data_efficiency.yaml` - Test at varying training data percentages
- **Modified**: `benchmark_console.py` - Added `--result-prefix` and `--checkpoint-id` args
- **Modified**: `eeg_bench/utils/utils.py` - Updated `save_results()` filename generation
- **Modified**: `.gitignore` - Added exception for `sweep_configs/*.yaml`

## Test plan
- [x] Run `python run_lejepa_sweep.py --config sweep_configs/performance_over_training.yaml --dry-run` to verify experiment matrix

author: copilot
body:
The deployment workflow times out after 10 minutes because the repository is configured to "Deploy from a branch", triggering GitHub's automatic Jekyll workflow which gets stuck in `deployment_queued` state and blocks the custom Vite workflow.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`**: Added `timeout-minutes: 5` to deploy job to fail fast instead of waiting 10 minutes
- **`DEPLOYMENT_FIX.md`**: Updated documentation to explain the root cause and required repository settings change

## Root Cause

When Pages source is set to "Deploy from a branch":
1. GitHub auto-runs Jekyll "pages build and deployment" workflow
2. Jekyll workflow enters `deployment_queued` and never completes
3. Custom Vite workflow cannot deploy (only one active deployment allowed)
4. Deployment cancelled after 10 minutes

## Required Manual Fix

Repository owner must change: **Settings → Pages → Source → "GitHub Actions"**

This disables the Jekyll workflow and allows the custom workflow to run. Cannot be automated via PR.

body:
### Motivation
- The previous Pygame-based viewer failed to build on some platforms (Windows) due to SDL/Visual Studio/distutils issues, so replace it with a standard-library GUI to avoid dependency and build problems.
- Provide a lightweight, cross-platform live viewer that does not require installing `pygame` or extra build tools.
- Keep the GUI optional and simple for debugging and demonstration of the `RiskEnv` stepping loop.

### Description
- Add a new Tkinter-based viewer at `scripts/run_gui.py` that draws territories, edges, owner colors, troop counts, a header, and the last action while stepping a `RiskEnv` with a random policy.
- Implement circular layout position calculation, a render loop using `root.after`, and controls for pause/step/reset with keyboard bindings and buttons.
- Remove the `pygame` optional dependency from `pyproject.toml` and update the README usage example to invoke `python scripts/run_gui.py --delay 0.8`.
- Preserve the `--delay`, `--seed`, and `--auto-reset` options and the basic UI state tracking in a `GuiState` dataclass.

### Testing

body:
Google Maps `center` prop requires `{lat, lng}` format but was receiving `{latitude, longitude}`, causing `InvalidValueError: not a LatLng or LatLngLiteral with finite coordinates`. Additionally, ~50 TypeScript errors existed due to missing type definitions.

## Changes

**Type System**
- Added type definitions using shared `GroupWithDetails` and `Coordinates` types
- Typed all state variables, function parameters, and refs
- Created `PublicGroup` interface extending `GroupWithDetails` with optional `distance` field

**Coordinate Conversion**
- Added `toLatLng()` helper to convert between coordinate formats
- Added `isValidLocation()` and `isValidLatLng()` type guards
- Updated GoogleMap component to use converted coordinates

**Other Fixes**
- Fixed AdvancedMarkerElement cleanup (property assignment vs method call)
- Updated EmptyState component to use `actions` array prop
- Changed property references from `location`/`address` to `locationName`

## Example

```typescript
// Before: Direct assignment caused format mismatch
<GoogleMap center={mapCenter} ... />

// After: Converts {latitude, longitude} to {lat, lng}
<GoogleMap center={toLatLng(mapCenter) || { lat: 0, lng: 0 }} ... />

function toLatLng(location: Location | null): LatLng | null {
  if (!isValidLocation(location)) return null;
  return {
    lat: location.latitude,
    lng: location.longitude
  };
}
```

Both current location detection and address search now work correctly.

## Summary
- Add benchmarks comparing cuDF GPU performance against CPU-based Arrow compute kernels
- Add DataFusion integration benchmarks comparing GPU-accelerated vs CPU-only query execution
- Add TPC-H decision support benchmarks (all 22 queries at SF=10)
- Benchmarks cover sorting, filtering, group-by aggregations, and complex SQL queries
- Tests multiple data sizes: 10K, 100K, 1M rows + TPC-H SF=10 (~10GB)

## Benchmark Results

**Test Environment:**
- GPU: NVIDIA Tesla T4 (AWS g4dn.xlarge)
- CPU: Intel Xeon (4 vCPUs)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 12.6

### Sort Benchmarks

| Operation | Size | GPU (cuDF) | CPU (Arrow) | Speedup |
|-----------|------|------------|-------------|---------|
| Single column | 10K | 576µs | 267µs | 0.5x |
| Single column | 100K | 1.97ms | 3.23ms | **1.6x** |
| Single column | 1M | 13.5ms | 40.7ms | **3.0x** |
| Multi column | 10K | 821µs | 641µs | 0.8x |
| Multi column | 100K | 2.38ms | 8.13ms | **3.4x** |
| Multi column | 1M | 18.0ms | 128ms | **7.1x** |

### GroupBy Benchmarks

| Operation | Size | GPU (cuDF) | CPU (HashMap) | Speedup |
|-----------|------|------------|---------------|---------|
| SUM | 100K | 1.27ms | 1.62ms | **1.3x** |
| SUM | 1M | 6.8ms | 16.2ms | **2.4x** |
| Multi-agg (SUM/MIN/MAX/COUNT) | 100K | 1.59ms | 2.21ms | **1.4x** |
| Multi-agg (SUM/MIN/MAX/COUNT) | 1M | 7.5ms | 22.1ms | **2.9x** |
| MEAN | 100K | 1.32ms | 1.65ms | **1.3x** |
| MEAN | 1M | 6.9ms | 16.5ms | **2.4x** |

### Filter Benchmarks

| Selectivity | Size | GPU (cuDF) | CPU (Arrow) | Speedup |
|-------------|------|------------|-------------|---------|
| 50% | 100K | 1.63ms | 622µs | 0.4x |
| 50% | 1M | 10.4ms | 7.3ms | 0.7x |

*Note: Filter benchmarks include GPU memory transfer overhead. For data already on GPU, performance would be better.*

### DataFusion Integration Benchmarks

Comparing DataFusion queries with GPU acceleration (via libcudf-datafusion) against CPU-only execution.

| Query Type | Size | GPU (cuDF) | CPU (DataFusion) | Speedup |
|------------|------|------------|------------------|---------|
| Sort | 1M | 128.9ms | 130.1ms | ~1.0x |
| Filter | 1M | 4.01ms | 4.02ms | ~1.0x |
| Aggregate | 1M | 5.53ms | 5.52ms | ~1.0x |
| Complex* | 1M | 7.41ms | 7.49ms | ~1.0x |

*Complex = Filter + Aggregate + Sort + LIMIT

### TPC-H Benchmarks (SF=10, ~10GB dataset)

All 22 TPC-H decision support queries:

| Query | GPU (cuDF) | CPU (DataFusion) | Speedup |
|-------|------------|------------------|---------|
| Q01 | 3.79s | 3.79s | ~1.0x |
| Q02 | 5.22s | 5.16s | ~1.0x |
| Q03 | 1.40s | 1.39s | ~1.0x |
| Q04 | 1.77s | 1.77s | ~1.0x |
| Q05 | 2.77s | 2.76s | ~1.0x |
| Q06 | 816ms | 819ms | ~1.0x |
| Q07 | 4.99s | 5.00s | ~1.0x |
| Q08 | 4.95s | 4.94s | ~1.0x |
| Q09 | 6.29s | 6.28s | ~1.0x |
| Q10 | 2.89s | 2.89s | ~1.0x |
| Q11 | 639ms | 639ms | ~1.0x |
| Q12 | 1.63s | 1.63s | ~1.0x |
| Q13 | 2.41s | 2.40s | ~1.0x |
| Q14 | 630ms | 628ms | ~1.0x |
| Q15 | 1.26s | 1.27s | ~1.0x |
| Q16 | 404ms | 404ms | ~1.0x |
| Q17 | 4.73s | 4.73s | ~1.0x |
| Q18 | 6.90s | 6.87s | ~1.0x |
| Q19 | 1.68s | 1.68s | ~1.0x |
| Q20 | 1.29s | 1.29s | ~1.0x |
| Q21 | 6.52s | 6.50s | ~1.0x |
| Q22 | 508ms | 508ms | ~1.0x |

## Key Findings

1. **Raw cuDF operations show 2-7x speedups** - Direct GPU sorting and aggregations outperform CPU at scale (100K+ rows)
2. **DataFusion integration shows ~1.0x** - Data transfer overhead (CPU↔GPU) offsets GPU compute benefits
3. **TPC-H at SF=10 shows ~1.0x** - Even with 10GB datasets, transfer overhead dominates for query workloads starting from CPU data
4. **GPU benefits require data locality** - Best speedups when data is already on GPU or for repeated operations on same data

## Files Added
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/common.rs` - Shared test data generation
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/sort_benchmark.rs` - Sort benchmarks
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/filter_benchmark.rs` - Filter benchmarks  
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/groupby_benchmark.rs` - GroupBy benchmarks
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/parquet_benchmark.rs` - Parquet I/O benchmarks
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/datafusion_benchmark.rs` - DataFusion GPU vs CPU benchmarks
- `libcudf-benchmarks/benches/tpch_benchmark.rs` - TPC-H benchmarks (all 22 queries)
- `libcudf-benchmarks/BENCHMARKS.md` - Results documentation

## Running Benchmarks
```bash
# Run all benchmarks
cargo bench --package libcudf-benchmarks

# Run specific benchmarks
cargo bench --package libcudf-benchmarks --bench sort_benchmark
cargo bench --package libcudf-benchmarks --bench datafusion_benchmark
cargo bench --package libcudf-benchmarks --bench tpch_benchmark
```

## Test plan
- [x] Build benchmarks: `cargo build --package libcudf-benchmarks --release`
- [x] Run benchmarks on GPU machine (Tesla T4)
- [x] Run DataFusion integration benchmarks
- [x] Run TPC-H benchmarks (all 22 queries at SF=10)
- [x] Document results

## What Does this PR Do?

Fixed two RLS policy conditions that incorrectly used camelCase column names instead of snake_case, which would cause policies to fail at runtime. PostgreSQL stores column and table names in snake_case/lowercase, so the policies must reference them correctly.

Changes:
- paymentMethods.ts: `"customerId"` → `"customer_id"`
- subscriptionItems.ts: `"subscriptionId"` → `"subscription_id"` and `"Subscriptions"` → `"subscriptions"`

The registry is already integrated with ComfyUI-Manager, and we want it to be the default place users install nodes from eventually. We do a security-scan of every node to improve safety. Feel free to read up more on the registry [here](https://docs.comfy.org/registry/overview#introduction)

- [ ] Merge the separate Github Actions PR, then merge this PR.

If you want to publish the node manually, [install the cli](https://docs.comfy.org/comfy-cli/getting-started#install-cli) by running `pip install comfy-cli`, then run `comfy node publish`

Otherwise, if you have any questions, please message me on discord at robinken or join our [server](https://discord.com/invite/comfyorg)!

Additionally, the UI for displaying battery, Bluetooth, and audio output information is streamlined, and necessary dependencies are updated.

**Codebase simplification and fetch logic centralization:**
- Refactored multiple components (`AudioOutputSelector`, `BatteryDisplay`, `BluetoothDisplay`, `DateTimeCard`) to use a shared `fetcher` utility instead of duplicating fetch and AsyncStorage logic for API calls, improving maintainability and consistency. **UI and feature enhancements:**

author: vgodsoe
body:
Our self-hosted runners are removed after 14 days of inactivity. This PR adds 2 workflows: 
1) Pulses each self-hosted runner to make sure it's alive. Generates an artifact if it is. This is scheduled to run on Sunday's at 1AM.
2) Pulls the artifacts and checks if any is missing. If one is missing, a message is created to notify the Lemonade team that a runner is down and needs maintenance. This runs Monday at 1AM so reports are ready for review.

author: larsartmann
body:
## Summary

• Fixed grep tool hanging with "Working..." status indefinitely when context is cancelled
• Added proper context cancellation support to `searchFilesWithRegex()` function
• Tool now properly cleans up when user cancels or context is cancelled

## Problem

When Grep tool uses its regex fallback implementation (when ripgrep is unavailable), it can hang indefinitely with UI showing "Working..." status. This happens because:

1. `searchFilesWithRegex()` did not accept a `context.Context` parameter
2. The `filepath.Walk()` callback never checked if context was cancelled
3. The function can take minutes to complete on large codebases (reads 512 bytes from every file to detect if it's text)
4. When context is cancelled, function never returns, leaving's `activeRequests` map with a cancel function
5. `IsBusy()` returns `true` as long as `activeRequests` contains a cancel function, so UI shows "Working..." forever

## Root Cause

The UI displays "Working..." when `AgentCoordinator.IsBusy()` returns true. This happens when `activeRequests` map contains a cancel function for a session. The cancel function is added when a tool starts and removed via `defer` when it completes. Since `searchFilesWithRegex()` never completes when context is cancelled, defer never runs, and `activeRequests` never gets cleaned up.

## Solution

Modified `searchFilesWithRegex()` function to:

1. **Accept a context.Context parameter** - Allows cancellation to propagate through the function
2. **Check context cancellation in filepath.Walk callback** - Aborts walk immediately when context is cancelled
3. **Check context after Walk completes** - Catches cancellations that happened late in the process
4. **Pass context through call chain** - `searchFiles()` → `searchFilesWithRegex(ctx, ...)`

Bonus fix: Improved error handling using `errors.Is()` instead of direct comparison for EOF checks.

## Testing

- ✅ All existing grep tests pass
- ✅ All tools tests pass (5.573s)
- ✅ Project builds successfully

## Files Changed

- `internal/agent/tools/grep.go` - Added context support and cancellation checks
- `internal/agent/tools/grep_test.go` - Updated tests to pass context

body:
Replaced minimal placeholder content with complete documentation for the Shiny R application that enables users to draw probability distributions and classifies them using ML.

## Documentation Added

- **Overview**: Interactive canvas interface for drawing → parameter estimation workflow
- **Distribution Support**: Documents 25+ distributions across continuous (Normal, Gamma, Beta, etc.), discrete (Binomial, Poisson, etc.), and multivariate (Wishart, Dirichlet, LKJ) families
- **Architecture**: Neural Network classifier with ImageInput → ImageBlock → ClassificationHead pipeline
- **Installation**: Complete R package dependencies and setup instructions
- **Technical Details**: 
  - Custom distribution implementations (`dCustomHalfCauchy`, `dCustomInverseChiSquared`, `dCustomBetaBinomial`)
  - Dual image naming conventions for training vs. generated samples
  - Code generation support for R, Python, Stan, Julia, Matlab, Mathematica, C++
- **Project Structure**: Annotated directory tree showing training data organization by distribution type

## Key Sections

```
Bayesian_Prior_Viz/
├── app.R                    # Main Shiny application
├── train/                   # Training images organized by distribution
│   ├── normal/
│   ├── beta/
│   └── ...
├── image_classifier/        # Neural network graph (JSON)
└── code_*.R                # Multi-language code generators
```

Transforms 1-line placeholder into 235 lines of actionable documentation covering installation, usage, and technical implementation details.

author: sfllaw
body: Recently, the golangci-lint workflow has been taking longer and longer to complete, causing it to timeout after the default of 5 minutes. Running error: context loading failed: failed to load packages: failed to load packages: failed to load with go/packages: context deadline exceeded Timeout exceeded: try increasing it by passing --timeout option Although PR #18398 enabled the Go module cache, bootstrapping with a cold cache still takes too long. This PR doubles the default 5 minute timeout for golangci-lint to 10 minutes so that golangci-lint can finish downloading all of its dependencies. Note that this doesn’t affect the 5 minute timeout configured in .golangci.yml, since running golangci-lint on your local instance should still be plenty fast. Fixes #18366

author: brianhelba
body:
* Add missing `__init__.py`  files to tasks
  * These are essential to making these into actual importable modules. Otherwise, they will be considered to be "implicit namespace modules", which have different behavior in subtle ways.
* Move tasks below the `bats_ai.core` package
  * This is the canonical location for Celery tasks in Resonant.
  * This is necessary to make `app.autodiscover_tasks()` work properly, as it scans the `INSTALLED_APPS` (in this case, `core`) for a `tasks` module. Perhaps this also wasn't working before due to the lack of `__init__.py`, so `tasks` wasn't considered a real module.
* Use `@app.task` instead of `@shared_task`
  * Previously, `@shared_task` was preferred by Resonant, but I realized that `@app.task` will be able to provide better typechecking. `@shared_task` is essential only for reusable apps (and `core` isn't reusable). I'll make an upstream change to the Resonant cookiecutter to prefer `@app.task` too.

body:
Controllers manually mapped `ZodError.issues` into flat arrays. Migrated to Zod v4's `z.flattenError()` for structured, field-keyed error responses.

## Changes

**Backend**
- Created `formatZodError()` utility wrapping `z.flattenError()`
- Updated ServiceController, FeatureFlagController, OrganizationController to use new utility
- Added `formatZodErrorTree()` for deeply nested schemas

**Frontend**
- Enhanced `errorUtils.ts` to parse both formats:
  ```typescript
  // Old: { details: [{ field: 'name', message: '...' }] }
  // New: { details: { fieldErrors: { name: ['...'] } } }
  ```
- Added `getValidationErrors()` helper returning field-keyed error map

**Tests**
- Added helper functions `hasFieldError()` and `hasErrorMessage()` to handle new structure
- Updated validation.test.ts and normalization.test.ts assertions

## Format Comparison

**Before:**
```json
{
  "error": "Validation failed",
  "details": [
    { "field": "name", "message": "String must contain at least 2 character(s)" },
    { "field": "port", "message": "Number must be greater than 0" }
  ]
}
```

**After:**
```json
{
  "error": "Validation failed",
  "details": {
    "formErrors": [],
    "fieldErrors": {
      "name": ["String must contain at least 2 character(s)"],
      "port": ["Number must be greater than 0"]
    }
  }
}
```

Frontend maintains backward compatibility during transition.

body:
## Summary

Changes `seek(0, true)` to `seek(0, false)` in the `selectTrack()` method to fix video sample extraction.

The debug panel showed audio working (1218 samples received) but video not working (0 samples received). The hypothesis is that `seek(0, true)` seeks to the nearest Random Access Point (keyframe), which might not be at time 0 for video tracks. For audio, every sample is typically a "keyframe", so it works. For video, the first keyframe might be at a later time, causing samples before it to be skipped.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Critical: Test on Tesla browser** - This fix cannot be verified without Tesla hardware. Check if the debug panel now shows non-zero "Samples Received" for the Video Demuxer section.
- [ ] **Verify mp4box.js documentation** - Confirm that `seek(time, useRap)` with `useRap=false` seeks to exact time without looking for keyframes.
- [ ] **Check video actually plays** - Verify video frames render and "Chunks Decoded" / "Frames Rendered" increment.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Deploy preview to Vercel
2. Open on Tesla browser
3. Press play and observe debug panel
4. Check Video Demuxer "Samples Received" - should now be > 0
5. Verify video frames render on canvas

### Notes

This is a hypothesis-based fix that cannot be verified without Tesla hardware. The change only affects the initial track selection, not user-initiated seeking during playback.

**Link to Devin run:** https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c3dae51828ae4a538396765d9a8fb205

body:
### Motivation
- Turn the existing fogorow/motorola device tree into a FOSSiBOT F106 Pro (`F106_Pro`) device target and remove Motorola-specific artifacts not needed for FOSSiBOT. 
- Use real FOSSiBOT device kernel configuration so the kernel build for `android_kernel_alps-5.10` matches the F106 Pro device. 
- Ensure mt6768 common configs and packaging reference the new device/vendor names so common blobs, HALs and init fragments are applied correctly. 
- Clean up vendor metadata and init/vintf entries that were Motorola-specific and either retarget or delete them. 

### Description
- Retargeted device/vendor names and paths from `motorola/fogorow` to `fossibot/f106pro` and replaced product identifiers (`device.mk`, `BoardConfig.mk`, `AndroidProducts.mk`, `lineage_*` files and related makefiles). 
- Added the real device kernel defconfig at `arch/arm64/configs/f106pro_defconfig` and wired it into MTK build configs by setting `KERNEL_DEFCONFIG` in `BoardConfig.mk` and `DEFCONFIG=f106pro_defconfig` in `build.config.mtk.aarch64*`. 
- Removed Motorola-only blobs and vendor init/manifest pieces, and retargeted proprietary-file mappings and vendor blueprints to `vendor/fossibot/f106pro`; updated extraction and patch rules (e.g. fingerprint service remap to `-fossibot`) in `extract-files.sh` and `proprietary-files.txt`. 
- Updated mt6768-common: narrowed `TARGET_DEVICE` checks to `F106_Pro`, renamed partition group identifiers and lights HAL/service to `fossibot` (code, rc and Soong entries), and removed `moto`/`motorola` references in common configs. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes. 
- The repository changes were staged and committed locally to validate file operations and applied patches. 
- Basic file-level consistency checks (renames/patch application) were performed by the rollout tooling and succeeded. 
- Further build and device-level testing (kernel build, vendor extraction, runtime verification) was not executed as part of this PR.

author: robinjhuang
body:
Hey! My name is Robin and I'm from [comfy-org](https://comfy.org/)! We would love to have you join the Comfy Registry, a public collection of custom nodes which lets authors publish nodes by version and automate testing against existing workflows.

The registry is already integrated with ComfyUI-Manager, and we want it to be the default place users install nodes from eventually. We do a security-scan of every node to improve safety. Feel free to read up more on the registry [here](https://docs.comfy.org/registry/overview#introduction)

- The documentation scaffolding? You can just add the example markdown [here](https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/help_page#setup) into web/docs/MyNode.md

Action Required:

- [ ] Go to the [registry](https://registry.comfy.org). Login and create a publisher id (everything after the `@` sign on your registry profile).
- [ ] Add the publisher id into the pyproject.toml file.
- [ ] Merge the separate Github Actions PR, then merge this PR.

If you want to publish the node manually, [install the cli](https://docs.comfy.org/comfy-cli/getting-started#install-cli) by running `pip install comfy-cli`, then run `comfy node publish`

Otherwise, if you have any questions, please message me on discord at robinken or join our [server](https://discord.com/invite/comfyorg)!

author: robinjhuang
body:
This PR adds a Github Action (publish-node-action) that will publish an updated version of your custom node to the [registry](https://registry.comfy.org/) whenever the `pyproject.toml` file changes. The pyproject.toml defines the custom node version you want to publish (added in another PR). Make sure you update the version number in `pyproject.toml` when you make a change that should be published to everyone!

Action Required:

- [ ] Make sure the trigger branch (`master` or `main`) in `publish.yaml` matches the branch you want to use as the publishing branch. It will only trigger when the pyproject.toml gets updated on that branch.
- [ ] Create an api key on the Registry for publishing from Github. [Instructions](https://docs.comfy.org/registry/publishing#create-an-api-key-for-publishing).
- [ ] Add it to your Github Repository Secrets as `REGISTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

Please message me on Discord at robinken or join our [server](https://discord.com/invite/comfyorg) server if you have any questions!

author: nawafswe
body:
## Motivation

Currently, many e2e tests use hardcoded YAML strings and `fmt.Sprintf`-based helper functions to create test resources. This approach has several drawbacks:

1. **Function name bloat**: As noted in [#11279](https://github.com/kumahq/kuma/issues/11279#issuecomment-xxx), this leads to unwieldy function names like `MTLSMeshWithMeshServicesAndMetricsKubernetes` when we need to support various field combinations.

2. **Maintainability**: Static YAML strings scattered throughout test files are harder to maintain and refactor when resource schemas change.

3. **Type safety**: String-based YAML generation lacks compile-time validation and IDE support.

This PR addresses these issues by replacing static YAML strings with the existing builder pattern that's already used in unit tests, following the approach suggested in the issue comments.

## Changes

This PR replaces hardcoded YAML strings with builder functions in e2e tests:

- **`test/e2e_env/multizone/localityawarelb/meshmultizoneservice.go`**: Replaced static `MeshMultiZoneService` YAML with `builders.MeshMultiZoneService()` builder pattern using method chaining.

- **`test/e2e_env/multizone/externalservices/externalservices_multizone_universal.go`**: Fixed incorrect usage of `ResourceUniversal()` to properly use the builder pattern.

## Benefits

- **Better maintainability**: Changes to resource schemas are easier to propagate through tests
- **Type safety**: Compile-time validation and IDE autocomplete support
- **Readability**: Fluent builder API is more readable than YAML strings
- **Consistency**: Aligns e2e tests with the builder pattern already used in unit tests
- **Extensibility**: Easy to add new field combinations without creating new function variants

## Future work

This PR focuses on `MeshMultiZoneService` as a starting point. Additional resources (such as `MeshLoadBalancingStrategy`) still use static YAML and can be migrated in follow-up PRs as builders become available.

## Related issues

Addresses [#11294](https://github.com/kumahq/kuma/issues/11294) and the concerns raised in [#11279](https://github.com/kumahq/kuma/issues/11279).

author: langesi
body:
## Summary
Add GIAS establishment `type_code: "08"` (Non-Maintained Special School) to our type mapping to prevent import jobs failing on this value.

## What changed
- Added mapping entry:
  - `non_maintained_special_school: "08"`

## Why
Our GIAS import currently does not recognise `type_code "08"`, which causes Sidekiq import jobs to fail/retry when a school with this code appears in the feed.

## How to verify
- In staging/dev, run (or retry) the GIAS import for data containing a school with `type_code: "08"` and confirm:
  - the import completes successfully
  - Sidekiq no longer shows failures for the import job(s)

## Impact / Risk
- Very low: this is a small additive enum/mapping entry (no behavioural change beyond recognising an existing official code).

## Related
- Trello: https://trello.com/c/h932UwpE

## Summary
- Implementar workflow de CI/CD para releases automáticos con detección de backends

author: farbdose
body:
### Motivation
- Avoid creating a `RenderType` during class static initialization to prevent early access to rendering internals at bootstrap time.
- Ensure shader and texture callbacks (`getSkyShader` / `setSkyTexture`) are wired when the render type is created.
- Move the dependency on `RenderType` to a safe client lifecycle point (client setup) to avoid referencing `LevelRenderer`/`RenderType` too early.

### Description
- Replace the static `SKY_RENDER_TYPE` with a nullable `skyRenderType` field and a lazy getter `LSBClient.getSkyRenderType()` that calls `RenderType.create(...)` on first use (file `LSBClient.java`).
- Assign the sky projection render type during `FMLClientSetupEvent` by calling `LSBClient.getSkyRenderType()` in `LSBClientModEventHandler.setup(...)` (file `LSBClientModEventHandler.java`).
- Update `LevelRendererMixin` to call `LSBClient.getSkyRenderType()` when ending the sky buffer batch instead of referencing the old static field (file `LevelRendererMixin.java`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.
